'''Edward King Bass IV''' (born July 14th, 1998), known professionally as '''Edward Skeletrix''', is an American conceptual artist, known for his work in [[music]], [[photography]], [[clothing]], and [[performance art]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Edward Skeletrix’s compelling Museum Music gives conceptual art a bad rap |url=https://www.thefader.com/2025/01/28/edward-skeletrix-museum-music-im-a-monster-review |access-date=2026-01-21 |website=The FADER |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Pierre |first=Alphonse |date=January 24, 2025 |title=Edward Skeletrix: Museum Music |url=https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/edward-skeletrix-museum-music/ |access-date=February 10, 2025 |website=[[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Barlas |first=Jon |date=January 23, 2025 |title=25 Rappers To Watch In 2025 |url=https://www.complex.com/music/a/dimassanfiorenzo/best-new-rappers-2025 |access-date=February 10, 2025 |website=[[Complex Networks|Complex]] |language=en}}</ref><ref name="032c" /> He began producing instrumental music in 2013 under the name Cight, and founded the clothing brand Syckli in 2018. He gained wider recognition in 2023 after uploading a series of [[Text-to-video model|AI-generated promotional materials]] to [[TikTok]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-11-16 |title=What is Skeletrix Island? Creepy AI-generated videos take over TikTok |url=https://www.yahoo.com/lifestyle/skeletrix-island-creepy-ai-generated-172845335.html |access-date=2026-01-21 |website=Yahoo Life |language=en-US}}</ref> That same year, he released his debut project ''Skeletrix Language.'' He subsequently released ''[[Museum Music]]'' in January 2025 and ''[[Body of Work (album)|Body of Work]]'' in May 2026. 

== Personal life ==
Edward King Bass IV<ref name=":4">{{Cite news |date=January 4, 2025 |title=From Nosferatu to Patience: a complete guide to this week's entertainment in the UK |url=https://www.theguardian.com/culture/2025/jan/04/nosferatu-patience-robbie-williams-2073bernard-butler--francis-bacon |access-date=February 10, 2025 |work=[[The Guardian]] |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> was born in 1998<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Cole |first=Alexander |date=January 2, 2025 |title=Edward Skeletrix Re-Invents The Wheel With His "Museum Music" Projects Released Under Different Names |url=https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/873361-edward-skeletrix-museum-music-stream |access-date=February 10, 2025 |website=[[HotNewHipHop]] |language=en}}</ref> in [[Florida]].<ref name=":1" /> He grew up in [[Albany, Georgia|Albany]], [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]]. His father, Edward King Bass III, is a doctor in Albany. Bass attended [[Georgia State University]] from 2016 to 2020 and earned a B.A. in Public Health.<ref>{{Cite web |title=CV |url=https://edwardkingbassiv.com/pages/return-policy |access-date=2026-05-19 |website=Edward King Bass IV |language=en}}</ref>

During college, Bass worked in a Baltimore-area [[psychiatric hospital]]. Bass has stated that his experiences working in psychiatric care influenced his artistic development and interest in consciousness, meditation, and mental health.<ref name="032c" />. In 2026, Bass revealed his history of mental illness, including [[derealization]], and an intense fear of developing [[schizophrenia]] that peaked during the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. He has cited [[Eckhart Tolle]] and [[Mooji]] as major influences on his personal philosophy.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o6IJY2P2-uo |title=Everything is Ok .. |date=2026-05-18 |last=Edward Skeletrix |access-date=2026-05-20 |via=YouTube}}</ref>

== Career ==
Bass began making music in 2013, [[Record producer|producing]] under the name ''Cight'', collaborating with rappers [[Night Lovell]] and [[XXXTentacion]].<ref name=":2" /> Bass was also a founding member of underground production groups 0% boys and Mizustation. Bass created the [[streetwear]] brand Syckli in late 2018.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Medithi |first=Vivian |date=January 28, 2025 |title=Edward Skeletrix's compelling Museum Music gives conceptual art a bad rap |url=https://www.thefader.com/2025/01/28/edward-skeletrix-museum-music-im-a-monster-review |access-date=February 10, 2025 |website=[[The Fader]] |language=en}}</ref> In mid-2019, Bass adopted the moniker "Edward Skeletrix" and in 2023 began uploading [[AI-generated art|AI-generated]] memes to [[TikTok]], which quickly gained popularity.<ref name=":3" />

Bass began releasing singles in early 2023, and released his debut project, ''Skeletrix Language,'' in December of that year.<ref name=":0" /> Shortly afterward, he teased a project by the name of ''Skeletrix Islvnd Rvdix 66.7'', although it was never released.<ref name=":0" /> Following the release of ''Skeletrix Language'', Bass began teasing ''[[Museum Music]]''.<ref name=":2" /> In the final days of 2024, Edward Skeletrix held a [[Pop-up exhibition|pop-up art gallery]] in New York City to promote the album, during which he sat inside of a glass box while fans poured water on him, prodded him with provided objects, and attempted to light him on fire.<ref name=":3" /> Upon its release on January 1, 2025, ''Museum Music'' was met with mixed reception from music critics.<ref name=":0" /> 

Bass announced his third album, ''[[Body of Work (album)|Body of Work]]'', on June 23, 2025. Although it was initially scheduled for July 1, 2025, the release was delayed to March 2026 for unknown reasons. On July 14, 2025, in an interview with Our Generation Music, Bass accused longtime collaborator Brennan Jones of mental and physical abuse, stating that Jones threatened to "kill Edward in his sleep" and that he was "not well".<ref name=":5">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3tostHxebdY |title=Well Well Well... {{!}} Edward Skeletrix |date=2025-07-14 |last=Our Generation Music |access-date=2025-07-15 |via=YouTube}}</ref>

From November 15-18 2025, Bass hosted a series of three exhibits titled ''Jester's Privilege''. The exhibits (''War, Perfect Animal, Mother of My Child?'') featured art from Bass, as well as [[performance art]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=NAMSKI |url=https://www.namski.com/jesters-privilege/home |access-date=2026-05-03 |website=www.namski.com}}</ref> Bass also contributed artwork to a January 2026 exhibit organized by Setareh Gallery in London, ''Breach''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Breach {{!}} Exhibitions {{!}} MutualArt |url=https://setareh-gallery.com/ |access-date=2026-05-03 |website=setareh-gallery.com |language=en}}</ref>

In early 2026, Bass announced that ''Body of Work'' had been further delayed to May 2026. The album's tracklist was revealed via an Instagram post on April 30, 2026, with the album releasing the following day. 

The album was accompanied by a broader multimedia campaign. Speaking to ''032c'', Bass described ''Body of Work'' as a "photo album", stating that the project was conceived through images as much as music and that each song was paired with its own artwork rather than a single album cover.<ref name="032c" /> The album's visual presentation featured collaborations with fashion designer [[Mowalola Ogunlesi|Mowalola]] and artist [[Pol Taburet]].<ref name="032c">{{Cite web |last=George |first=Cassidy |date=May 28, 2026 |title=Edward Skeletrix: The Mind as Masterpiece |url=https://magazine.032c.com/magazine/edward-skeletrix-the-mind-as-masterpiece |access-date=May 29, 2026 |website=[[032c]]}}</ref>

Bass hosted a multi-space installation and performance work in London on May 2, 2026, titled ''Commerce of Desire'', to promote ''Body of Work''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NAMSKI |url=https://www.namski.com/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260503004418/https://www.namski.com/ |archive-date=2026-05-03 |access-date=2026-05-03 |website=www.namski.com}}</ref>

Bass hosted an exhibition in Los Angeles, California on July 25, 2026, titled ''Analytica'', in collaboration with Illumitati and [[Weiland (musician)|Weiland]]. The exhibit was attended by artists such as [[Matt Proxy]], [[North West (musician)|North West]], Emwell, and Elijah Walker.

== Artistry ==
Bass's work has been associated with surreal and [[uncanny valley]] imagery, particularly in his use of AI-generated video and promotional material.<ref name=":3" /> ''032c'' described him as a "worldbuilder" whose practice spans music, photography, painting, fashion and performance, with Bass stating that music is "a piece of the world" rather than the sole focus of his work.<ref name="032c" /> Bass has said that he is interested in strong audience reactions and in art that appears unsettling while carrying a positive or meditative intention.<ref name="032c" />

Bass has cited [[Triad God]], [[XXXTentacion]], Slime Dollaz, [[Eckhart Tolle]], [[Mooji]], deadlydollaz, salon and cough, [[Arca (musician)|Arca]], and YAYAYI as influences.<ref name=":5" />

Bass's work as Edward Skeletrix has been cited as an influence by musicians such as [[Matt Proxy]].

DOGE official now running US Institute of Peace |url=https://www.newsweek.com/who-nate-cavanaugh-doge-official-now-running-us-institute-peace-2053170 |access-date=March 12, 2026 |website=Newsweek |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Barrett">{{Cite news |last=Barrett |first=Brian |title=Federal Judge Allows DOGE to Take Over $500 Million Office Building for Free |url=https://www.wired.com/story/judge-approves-doge-usip-office-building/|date=April 1, 2025 |access-date=March 12, 2026 |work=Wired |language=en-US |issn=1059-1028}}</ref>

In his role as a DOGE staffer, he was responsible for terminating nearly all of the grants at the [[National Endowment for the Humanities]] and is the subject of a lawsuit filed in 2026.<ref name="video-deposition" /><ref name="ACLS-AHA-MLA_20260306" /><ref name="AHA_20260307" /> 

Cavanaugh was also appointed acting director of the [[United States Interagency Council on Homelessness|Interagency Council on Homelessness]], and placed the agency's entire staff on administrative leave.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |last=Elliott |first=Vittoria |title=Where the DOGE Operatives Are Now |url=https://www.wired.com/story/where-the-doge-operatives-are-now/ |access-date=2026-05-13 |work=Wired |language=en-US |issn=1059-1028}}</ref>

== Career ==

=== Education ===
Cavanaugh was a 19-year-old student at [[Indiana University Bloomington|Indiana University]] when he dropped out of college. Cavanaugh is the son of Pat Cavanaugh, founder of Ready Nutrition.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Brainbase CEO Nate Cavanaugh on Striking Out as a Young CEO - dot.LA |url=https://dot.la/meet-the-24-year-old-trying-to-disrupt-the-intellectual-property-industry-2646319922.html |access-date=March 12, 2026 |website=dot.la |language=en}}</ref>

=== Second Trump administration ===
On March 12, 2025, Cavanaugh and fellow DOGE employee Justin Fox began overseeing the [[Department of Government Efficiency]]’s work with the [[National Endowment for the Humanities]] (NEH) after its chair, [[Shelly Lowe|Shelly C. Lowe]], left at President Donald Trump's direction and NEH general counsel [[Michael Patrick McDonald (born 1956)]] became acting chair.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Schuessler |first=Jennifer |date=March 7, 2026 |title=When DOGE Unleashed ChatGPT on the Humanities |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/03/07/arts/humanities-endowment-doge-trump.html |access-date=March 12, 2026 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Schuessler |first=Jennifer |date=March 12, 2025 |title=Chair of National Endowment for the Humanities Leaves at Trump’s ‘Direction’ |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/03/12/arts/national-endowment-humanities-trump-shelly-lowe.html |access-date=March 12, 2026 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Johansen |first=Ben |last2=Cai |first2=Sophia |last3=Sentner |first3=Irie |date=April 16, 2025 |title=DOGE comes for the little guy |url=https://www.politico.com/newsletters/west-wing-playbook-remaking-government/2025/04/16/doge-comes-for-the-little-guy-00294469 |access-date=March 12, 2026 |website=Politico |language=en}}</ref> 

Under Cavanaugh and Fox's leadership of the NEH, DOGE used [[ChatGPT]] to identify grants that were in violation of Trump's executive orders related to [[Diversity, equity, and inclusion|DEI]], ultimately terminating 97% of the agency's grants within 22 days.<ref name="Inside_Higher_Ed_20260311">{{Cite web |last=Custer |first=Sara |title=How DOGE Gutted the NEH in 22 Days |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/faculty-issues/research/2026/03/11/how-doge-gutted-neh-22-days |access-date=March 12, 2026 |website=Inside Higher Ed |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/tv/news/doge-justin-fox-dei-definition-video-b2936671.html |title=DOGE staffer who flagged grants for ‘DEI’ struggles with definition |date=March 11, 2026 |language=en |access-date=March 12, 2026 |work=The Independent}}</ref> Fox and Cavanaugh prompted the chat bot to answer in less than 120 characters.<ref name="DOGE-inside-look" />

In March 2025, after Cavanaugh was appointed president of the US Institute for Peace, he transferred ownership of the headquarters building to the [[General Services Administration]].<ref name="Barrett" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Klee |first=Miles |date=April 1, 2025 |title=Meet the Silicon Valley Zealot Leading the U.S. Institute of Peace |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/politics/politics-news/doge-us-institute-of-peace-nate-cavanaugh-1235307495/ |access-date=March 12, 2026 |website=Rolling Stone |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |first1=Avi |last1=Asher-Schapiro|first2=Christopher |last2=Bing|date=August 22, 2025 |title=DOGE Targeted Him on Social Media. Then the Taliban Took His Family. |url=https://www.propublica.org/article/doge-musk-mohammad-halimi-institute-peace-taliban |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=ProPublica |language=en-US}}</ref> On May 18, Cavanaugh's appointment was ruled unlawful by Judge [[Beryl Howell]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fields |first=Gary |date=May 19, 2025 |title=Judge bars Trump administration from shutting peace institute that sought to end violent conflicts |url=https://apnews.com/article/trump-doge-institute-of-peace-lawsuit-39d79077c8fa5336634d518f30a9a807 |access-date=May 19, 2025 |agency=[[Associated Press]] }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Lee |first=Ella |date=May 19, 2025 |title=Judge deems DOGE takeover of US Institute of Peace 'null and void' |url=https://thehill.com/regulation/court-battles/5307665-judge-nullifies-doge-takeover-usip/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250520025214/https://thehill.com/regulation/court-battles/5307665-judge-nullifies-doge-takeover-usip/ |archive-date=May 20, 2025 |access-date=May 19, 2025 |newspaper=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Barrett |first=Brian |title=DOGE Loses Battle to Take Over USIP—and Its $500 Million Headquarters |url=https://www.wired.com/story/usip-doge-headquarters-building-ruling/ |access-date=March 13, 2026 |work=Wired }}</ref>

Cavanaugh was deposed on January 23, 2026, as part of a lawsuit brought by the [[American Council of Learned Societies]], the [[American Historical Association]], and the [[Modern Language Association]] against the Trump administration in connection with his role in the termination of NEH grants.<ref name="video-deposition">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cvd1wggkB0Y |title=Nathan Cavanaugh Deposition in ACLS-AHA-MLA Lawsuit About the NEH, Part 5 of 6 |date=March 7, 2026 |last=American Historical Association |access-date=March 12, 2026 |via=YouTube}}</ref><ref name="ACLS-AHA-MLA_20260306">{{Cite web |title=ACLS-AHA-MLA Lawsuit: Discovery Materials |url=https://www.acls.org/acls-aha-mla-lawsuit-discovery-materials/ |access-date=12 March 2026 |website=[[American Council of Learned Societies]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web| title=Reed, Warren, Wyden Urge Investigation to Determine if DOGE Employees’ Committed Criminal Violations of Federal Ethics Laws {{!}} U.S. Senator Jack Reed of Rhode Island| access-date=2026-03-13| date=2025-05-29| url=https://www.reed.senate.gov/news/releases/reed-warren-wyden-urge-investigation-to-determine-if-doge-employees-committed-criminal-violations-of-federal-ethics-laws}}</ref> Videos of Cavanaugh and Fox's depositions went viral.<ref name="DOGE-inside-look">{{Cite web |last=Binder |first=Matt |date=2026-03-13 |title=Former DOGE employees give an inside look at the Elon Musk-led agency |url=https://mashable.com/article/former-doge-employees-deposition-inside-look-elon-musk-agency |access-date=2026-03-13 |website=Mashable |language=en}}</ref>

In subsequent court filings, the plaintiffs and NEH produced additional materials describing DOGE's involvement in grant terminations.<ref>{{Cite web| last=Algemeiner| first=The| title=DOGE Staffers Used ChatGPT to Cut Holocaust History Grants During Counter-DEI Purges: Lawsuit| work=Algemeiner.com| access-date=2026-03-13| url=https://www.algemeiner.com/2026/03/10/doge-staffers-used-chatgpt-cut-holocaust-history-grants-during-counter-dei-purges-lawsuit/}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web| last=Societies| first=American Council of Learned| title=Discovery Released in Lawsuit by Humanities Groups Reveals ChatGPT-Powered Process by DOGE in Cancelling Grants for Schools, Libraries, and Community Organizations| access-date=2026-03-13| url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/discovery-released-in-lawsuit-by-humanities-groups-reveals-chatgpt-powered-process-by-doge-in-cancelling-grants-for-schools-libraries-and-community-organizations-302707495.html}}</ref><ref name="Inside_Higher_Ed_20260311"/>

Discovery materials in the lawsuit state that Cavanaugh, as part of a small DOGE team including Fox, advised NEH leadership on identifying previously awarded grants for possible termination under Trump administration executive orders and that DOGE staff used spreadsheet keyword searches and the ChatGPT language model to help flag projects for review.<ref name="AHA_20260307">{{Cite web| title=Major Update in our NEH Lawsuit|work=[[American Historical Association]]|date=March 7, 2026| access-date=2026-03-13| url=https://www.historians.org/news/major-update-in-our-neh-lawsuit/}}</ref> Cavanaugh admitted that the DOGE team was not successful in reducing the deficit, but that he did not regret harming the livelihood of those whose grants he was involved in terminating. <ref>{{Cite web |title=2 DOGE staffers say 'no' regrets for people losing income, didn't reduce the deficit: Depositions |url=https://abcnews.com/Politics/2-doge-staffers-regrets-people-losing-income-reduce/story?id=131050170 |access-date=2026-03-23 |website=ABC News |language=en}}</ref>

On March 13, 2026, judge [[Colleen McMahon]] of the Federal District Court in Manhattan ordered the viral videos of Fox and Cavanaugh's depositions to be taken down, ordering the scholarly groups "take any and all possible steps to claw back” the videos.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Weiser |first=Benjamin |last2=Schuessler |first2=Jennifer |date=2026-03-13 |title=After DOGE Deposition Videos Go Viral, Judge Orders Them Taken Down |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/03/13/nyregion/doge-depositions-musk-lawsuit.html |access-date=2026-03-13 |work=The New York Times }}</ref> Ten days later, Judge McMahon lifted her order, ruling that the risk of "embarrassment and reputational harm" was not enough to overcome the public interest in Cavanaugh's and Fox's descriptions of their official conduct.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Charalambous |first=Peter |date=March 23, 2026 |title=Judge allows release of deposition videos of 2 former DOGE staffers |url=https://abcnews.com/US/judge-allows-release-deposition-videos-2-former-doge/story?id=131335670 |access-date=2026-03-24 |website=ABC News |language=en}}</ref>

In May 2026, Judge McMahon ruled that DOGE's cancellation of the humanities grants was unconstitutional, calling it "a textbook example of unconstitutional viewpoint discrimination".<ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-05-08 |title=Judge finds Trump's DOGE-led cancellation of humanities grants unconstitutional |url=https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/judge-finds-trumps-doge-led-cancellation-of-humanities-grants-unconstitutional |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260512170744/https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/judge-finds-trumps-doge-led-cancellation-of-humanities-grants-unconstitutional |archive-date=2026-05-12 |access-date=2026-05-15 |work=PBS News |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Private sector ===
In April 2026, ''Wired'' published an investigation titled "Where the DOGE Operatives Are Now".<ref name=":1" /> According to the investigation, both Cavanaugh and his former subordinate Justin Fox are currently employed at Special, an AI startup to bring "DOGE for the private sector."<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite news |last=Elliott |first=Vittoria |title=The DOGE Boys Get VC Funding to Support Their Latest Enterprise |url=https://www.wired.com/story/the-doge-boys-get-vc-funding-to-support-their-latest-enterprise/ |access-date=2026-06-06 |work=Wired |language=en-US |issn=1059-1028}}</ref>

On June 3, 2026, Cavanaugh announced the launch of Special on ''X'', with backing from [[Marc Andreessen|Marc Andreessen’s]] venture capital firm [[Andreessen Horowitz|a16z]]. In a post on a16z’s Substack, Cavanaugh and Fox wrote that Special will build "an operating system to transform critical American industries with AI."<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Warzel |first=Charlie |date=2026-06-10 |title=The DOGE Bros Want Another Shot |url=https://www.theatlantic.com/technology/2026/06/doge-special-figure-health/687493/ |access-date=2026-06-10 |website=The Atlantic |language=en}}</ref>

'''Patrick Marron Ball'''<ref name="Yale">{{cite web |title=2021 & 2022 Commencement Program |url=https://issuu.com/yalerep/docs/2021-22-program-web |website=[[Yale School of Drama|David Geffen School of Drama at Yale University]] |access-date=13 April 2025 |page=2 |date=23 May 2022 |via=[[Issuu]]}}</ref> (born November 10, 1989)<ref>{{cite web |last=Sarkar |first=Ishani |title=Who is Patrick Ball, the actor who plays Dr Frank Langdon in The Pitt? |url=https://www.scmp.com/magazines/style/people/celebrities/article/3340948/meet-patrick-ball-who-plays-dr-frank-langdon-hbo-maxs-pitt |website=[[South China Morning Post]] |access-date=27 January 2026 |date=23 January 2026}}</ref> is an American actor. He is best known for his role as Dr. [[Frank Langdon]] on the [[HBO Max]] [[medical drama]] television series ''[[The Pitt]]'' (2025–present), for which he has received critical acclaim and nominations for the [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Supporting Actor in a Drama Series]] and the [[Critics' Choice Television Award for Best Supporting Actor in a Drama Series]].<ref name="Pedersen-2026">{{Cite web |last1=Pedersen |first1=Erik |last2=Gomez |first2=Dessi |last3=Hipes |first3=Patrick |date=2026-07-08 |title=Emmy Nominations 2026: List Of Nominees |url=https://deadline.com/lists/emmy-nominations-full-list-nominees-scorecard/ |access-date=2026-07-08 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood|Deadline]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Ball was born to Jim and Lee Ann Ball;<ref name="Johnson-2025">{{cite web |last=Johnson |first=Maria |title=Life's Funny |url=https://ohenrymag.com/lifes-funny-110/ |website=O.Henry Magazine |access-date=2 March 2026 |date=1 December 2025}}</ref> his father is a former paramedic and his mother is a former emergency room nurse.<ref>{{cite web |last=Rice |first=Lynette |title='The Pitt' Star Patrick Ball On His Character's Shocking Reveal & What Will Happen Next |url=https://deadline.com/2025/03/the-pitt-star-patrick-ball-langdon-drugs-1236312062/ |website=[[Deadline Hollywood|Deadline]] |access-date=13 April 2025 |date=7 March 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Jacobs |first=Meredith |title='The Pitt': Noah Wyle & Patrick Ball Break Down Major Robby & Langdon Fight |url=https://www.wfmz.com/entertainment/the-pitt-noah-wyle-patrick-ball-break-down-major-robby-langdon-fight/article_d8338111-c1c4-51ae-8352-5bd0104d36e8.html |website=[[WFMZ-TV|WFMZ]] |access-date=15 April 2025 |date=6 March 2025}}</ref> He has two younger siblings, one of whom works as an occupational therapist.<ref name="Johnson-2025" /><ref name="Simon-2026">{{cite web |last=Simon |first=Samantha |title=How Patrick Ball Found His Way to 'The Pitt' |url=https://www.lofficielusa.com/film-tv/patrick-ball-the-pitt-actor-interview-season-2-cast-dr-langdon-mel-king |website=[[L'Officiel USA]] |access-date=20 June 2026 |date=12 March 2026}}</ref> He is a descendant of the Ball family of [[Charleston, South Carolina|Charleston]], who owned farms where [[Carolina Gold]] rice was produced, and some of his ancestors are buried near [[Strawberry Chapel and Childsbury Town Site|Strawberry Chapel]]. Of his heritage, Ball said, "I'm still enjoying a lot of generational privileges that were afforded to me by that family history. It's something that my parents really thought it was important for us to acknowledge and understand."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Thompson |first=Marilyn W. |date=2025-12-30 |title=This actor whose family goes back to 17th-century Charleston is in Emmy-nominated 'The Pitt' |url=https://www.postandcourier.com/charleston_scene/theater/patrick-ball-the-pitt-medical-charleston-family/article_8c89c4db-72a3-40e1-904c-dbe66d39263d.html |access-date=2026-08-14 |website=[[The Post and Courier]] |language=en}}</ref> 

Ball grew up in [[Summerfield, North Carolina]], and attended [[Northwest Guilford High School]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Buchanan |first=Bruce |title=Triad Stage will present Preston Lane's 'The Passion of Teresa Rae King' |url=https://greensboro.com/entertainment/article_f58e64b7-ef71-5f32-bd5a-3b5e2cb58f0f.html |url-access=subscription |website=[[News & Record]] |access-date=15 April 2025 |date=26 |access-date=15 April 2025 |date=24 April 2005}}</ref><ref name="Clarey-2025">{{cite web |last=Clarey |first=Brian |title=Patrick Ball's Big Break athletics and theatre, though he did not view performing as a particular passion at this time.<ref name="Lee-2026">{{Cite web |last=Lee |first=Sophie |date=2026-04-07 |title=How The Pitt's Patrick graduating to pursue acting.<ref name="Rankin-2026">{{cite web |last=Rankin |first=Seija |title='The Pitt' Star Patrick Ball Was Happy to Bet on Himself |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-features/patrick-ball-the-pitt-season-2-dr-langdon-interview-1236501867/ |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |access-date=2 March 2026 |date=12 February 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Tauer |first=Kristen |date=2026-04-01 |title=Patrick Ball Goes From 'The Pitt' to His Broadway Debut in 'Becky Shaw' after a friend requested that he perform a 10-minute theatre scene; the head of the University of North Carolina at Greensboro's theatre department subsequently encouraged him to become an actor.<ref name="Lee-2026" />

After moving to [[New York City]] and spending five years acting in local theater productions throughout the United States, Ball received a [[Yale School of Drama#Degrees and certificates|Certificate in Drama]] from the [[David Geffen School of Drama at Yale University]] in 2022.<ref name="Yale" /><ref name="Clarey-2025" /> He auditioned to the program with [[Hamlet]]'s first soliloquy.<ref name="Willman-2025" /> That year, he also completed a [[Bachelor of Fine Arts|BFA]] from the [[University of North Carolina at Greensboro]], which allowed his Certificate in Drama to be converted to a [[Master of Fine Arts]] degree.<ref name="Clarey-2025" />

==Career==

=== Television ===
Following his debut as a guest on ''[[Law & Order]]'' in 2023, Ball's next work in television was playing Dr. [[Frank Langdon]] in the HBO Max medical drama ''The Pitt.''<ref name="Simon-2026" /> His casting was announced on July 12, 2024.<ref name="Otterson-2024">{{cite web |last=Otterson |first=Joe |title=Max Medical Procedural 'The Pitt' Starring Noah Wyle Sets Main Cast |url=https://variety.com/2024/tv/news/max-medical-procedural-the-pitt-noah-wyle-cast-1236069172/ |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |access-date=13 April 2025 |date=12 July 2024}}</ref> To prepare for the role, he spoke to real physicians and nurses who have experienced [[addiction]].<ref name="Rankin-2026" /> Reporting on Ball's portrayal of his character's journey towards [[sobriety]] and regaining his confidence in the emergency department, Shadan Larki for ''Awards Buzz'' praised his performance for its subtlety and restraint, which culminated into "an emotional payoff that feels fully earned."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Larki |first=Shadan |date=2026-06-10 |title=Interview: Patrick Ball on the Emotional Impact of ‘The Pitt’ and the Show’s Passionate Fan Response |url=https://awardsbuzz.com/patrick-ball-on-the-emotional-impact-of-the-pitt-and-the-shows-passionate-fan-response/ |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=Awards Buzz |language=en}}</ref> Ball was nominated for the [[Critics' Choice Television Award for Best Supporting Actor in a Drama Series]] for his role as Langdon.<ref name="Simon-2026" /> With his co-stars, he won the [[Actor Award for Outstanding Performance by an Ensemble in a Drama Series]] for 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nordyke |first=Kimberly |date=2026-03-02 |title=Actor Awards: Complete List of Winners December 2025.<ref>{{cite web |last=Cordero |first=Rosy |title='The Pitt' Star Patrick Ball Signs With Gersh |url=https://deadline.com/2025/12/the-pitt-patrick-ball-gersh-agency-1236636179/ |website=[[Deadline Hollywood|Deadline]] |access-date=8 July 2026 |date=4 December 2025}}</ref>

Ball starred as [[Prince Hamlet]] in [[Robert O'Hara]]'s production of ''[[Hamlet]]'' at the [[Mark Taper Forum]] from May to July 2025.<ref>{{cite web |last=Gelt |first=Jessica |title=From 'The Pitt' to 'Hamlet': Patrick Ball and a twisty take on Shakespeare come to the L.A. stage |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/story/2025-06-02/the-pitt-patrick-ball-hamlet-mark-taper-forum-robert-ohara-gina-torres |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |access-date=4 June 2025 |date=2 June 2025}}</ref><ref name="Willman-2025">{{cite web |last=Willman |first=Chris |title=Patrick Ball on Playing 'Hamlet' at the Mark Taper by Night, While Shooting 'The Pitt' Season 2 by Day: 'They're Both Disgraced Princes… I'm in My Prince Era Here' |url=https://variety.com/2025/legit/news/patrick-ball-hamlet-mark-taper-stage-pitt-langdon-1236418120/ |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |access-date=4 June 2025 |date=4 June 2025}}</ref> Ball had always wanted to participate in a production of ''Hamlet'', and prepared for the play by watching ''[[Mulholland Drive (film)|Mulholland Drive]]'' and ''[[The Big Clock (film)|The Big Clock]]''.<ref name="Willman-2025" /> Emily Parise praised Ball's balanced portrayal of Prince Hamlet, while Kevin Taft and Bruce R. ==Personal life==
Ball has been in a relationship with actress Elysia Roorbach since October 2023. She guest starred as a patient of his character on season 2 of ''The Pitt''.<ref>{{cite web |last=Raposas |first=Rachel |title=Patrick Ball Celebrates Girlfriend Elysia Roorbach's TV Debut Alongside Him on The Pitt: 'Killed it' |url=https://people.com/patrick-ball-girlfriend-elysia-roorbach-features-alongside-him-on-the-pitt-11888121 |website=[[People (magazine)|People]] |access-date=2 March 2026 |date=19 January 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Routhier |first=Ray |title=Maine actor makes her TV debut in current season of HBO Max's 'The Pitt' |url=https://www.pressherald.com/2026/01/21/maine-actor-makes-her-tv-debut-in-current-season-of-hbo-maxs-the-pitt/ |website=[[Portland Press Herald]] |access-date=2 March 2026 |date=21 January 2026}}</ref> They met while performing in a stage production of ''[[Las Aventuras de Juan Planchard|Las Adventuras de Juan Planchard]]'' in Miami.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lekic |first=Raquel |date=2026-04-22 |title=Patrick Ball's Girlfriend Elysia Roorbach Appeared on 'The Pitt' |url=https://www.womansworld.com/entertainment/celebrities/patrick-ball-and-girlfriend-elysia-roorbach-appear-on-the-pitt |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=[[Woman's World]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

Ball has experienced addiction. He faced suspensions throughout high school, and often did drugs recreationally.<ref name="Simon-2026" /> He was initially only accepted into the University of North Carolina at Greensboro's BFA program on probation due to his habit of drinking, partying, and being arrested.<ref name="Lee-2026" /> As of February 2026, he has been sober for four years.<ref name="Rankin-2026" />

Prior to his television success, Ball worked four jobs in New York, including in a coffee shop and as a wardrobe assistant for ''[[And Just Like That...]]''.<ref name="Lee-2026" /> He considered joining the [[FBI]], becoming a [[United States Merchant Marine|Merchant Marine]], and working in an Alaskan fishing camp in order to financially support himself.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ferri |first=Alessia |date=2026-04-10 |title=Patrick Ball Reveals 'The Pitt' Saved Him From $80,000 in Debt: "I Thought I Was Gonna Die With It" |url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/story/patrick-ball-reveals-the-pitt-saved-him-from-student-loan-debt |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]]}}</ref> While studying at the David Geffen School of Drama, his parents urged him to drop out and pursue a more stable career so he would not accumulate more debt.<ref name="Rankin-2026" /> After three months of working on ''The Pitt'', Ball was able to clear $80,000 worth of [[student debt]].<ref name="Lee-2026" /><ref>{{cite web |last=Sharf |first=Zack |title='The Pitt' Actor Patrick Ball Cries While Revealing Show Got Him Out of $80,000 Worth of Debt: 'I Thought I Was Gonna Die With It' |url=https://variety.com/2026/tv/news/patrick-ball-the-pitt-debt-1236711702/ |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |access-date=8 July 2026 |date=8 April 2026}}</ref>

'''Andrew Durand''' (born January 17, 1986)<ref name="auto3">{{cite web |url=https://www.ibdb.com/broadway-cast-staff/andrew-durand-488888 |title=Andrew Durand – Broadway Cast & Staff |website=IBDB |access-date=2025-10-05}}</ref> is an American actor, known for his roles on Broadway in ''[[Shucked]]'' and ''[[Dead Outlaw]]'', the latter for which he was nominated for the 2025 [[Tony Award for Best Leading Actor in a Musical]]. He has also received two [[Drama Desk Award]] nominations for ''Shucked'' and ''Dead Outlaw''.

== Early life ==
Originally from [[Roswell, Georgia]],<ref name="Marietta Times">{{cite news |title=Broadway's Andrew Durand, who plays a corpse in 'Dead Outlaw,' reveals the secret to stillness |url=https://www.mariettatimes.com/news/entertainment/2025/04/broadways-andrew-durand-who-plays-a-corpse-in-dead-outlaw-reveals-the-secret-to-stillness/ |access-date=17 June 2025 |publisher=Marietta Times |date=29 April 2025}}</ref> Durand started acting after seeing a play at the community theater Village Playhouses of Roswell.<ref name="ArtsATL">{{cite web |last1=Fuller |first1=Sally |title=Tony nominated 'Dead Outlaw' star Andrew Durand discovered theater as a kid in Roswell |url=https://www.artsatl.org/tony-nominated-dead-outlaw-star-andrew-durand-discovered-theater-as-a-kid-in-roswell/ |website=ArtsATL |date=5 June 2025 |access-date=17 June 2025}}</ref> Durand attended [[North Springs High School]] and [[Boston Conservatory at Berklee|Boston Conservatory]].<ref name="ArtsATL" /><ref name="Boston Conservatory">{{cite news |last1=Donahue |first1=Tori |title=Six Boston Conservatory Alumni Nominated for Tony Awards |url=https://bostonconservatory.berklee.edu/news/six-boston-conservatory-alumni-nominated-for-tony-awards |access-date=17 June 2025 |publisher=Boston Conservatory |date=1 May 2025}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{cite web |url=https://www.newyorktheatreguide.com/theatre-news/interviews/andrew-durand |title=Andrew Durand – Q & A |website=New York Theatre Guide |date=19 October 2017 |access-date=2025-10-05}}</ref>

==Career==
After graduating, Durand's first professional roles were in [[Boston]]. He played Fiddlin' John in ''[[Parade (musical)|Parade]]'' and Steve in ''[[Zanna, Don't!]]'' at the SpeakEasy Stage Company in 2007.<ref name="auto3"/>

The next year, he made his Broadway debut as a replacement for Georg in the Tony-winning production of ''[[Spring Awakening (musical)|Spring Awakening]]''.<ref name="playbill spring awakening">{{cite web |url=https://playbill.com/article/castanos-durand-karr-kinney-kinnunen-and-violett-join-broadways-spring-awakening-com-151851 |title=Castaños, Durand, Karr, Kinney, Kinnunen and Violett Join Broadway's Spring Awakening |website=Playbill |access-date=2025-10-05}}</ref> The next year, he joined the Off-Broadway production of ''The Burnt Part Boys'' and its transfer to [[Playwrights Horizons]]. The same year, he appeared in ''Yank!'' at [[York Theatre Company]]. Both of the plays he was in that year were in [[New York City|New York]].

In 2012, he joined the cast of the Tony-winning play ''[[War Horse (play)|War Horse]]'' as Albert Narracot.<ref name="auto2"/><ref name="auto4">{{cite web |url=https://www.broadway.com/buzz/159356/get-a-first-look-at-war-horses-new-leading-man-andrew-durand/ |title=Get a First Look at War Horse's New Leading Man, Andrew Durand |website=Broadway.com |access-date=2025-10-05}}</ref> In 2013, he performed as Boyet in [[The Public Theater]]'s production of ''[[Love's Labour's Lost]]'', as part of its summer Shakespeare in the Park series.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/lifestyle/style/loves-labours-lost-theater-review-604288/ |title='Love's Labour's Lost': Theater Review |author=Frank Scheck |date=2013-08-12 |website=The Hollywood Reporter |access-date=2025-10-05}}</ref>

His next Broadway appearance was his first time originating a role, playing Musidorus in the 2018 Broadway premiere of [[The Go-Go's]] jukebox musical ''[[Head Over Heels (musical)|Head Over Heels]]'', a role he played through the show's closing in 2019.<ref name="auto">{{cite web |url=https://www.broadwaybox.com/daily-scoop/seven-questions-with-head-over-heels-star-andrew-durand/ |title=Seven Questions With Head Over Heels Star Andrew Durand |website=BroadwayBox |access-date=2025-10-05}}</ref> He returned later in 2019 in the Broadway premiere of ''[[Ink (play)|Ink]]'', as Beverly/Christopher Timothy. The play was nominated for the [[Tony Award for Best Play]].

Durand's next role was in the 2023 Broadway premiere of ''[[Shucked]]'', a musical from [[Robert Horn (writer)|Robert Horn]], [[Brandy Clark]], and [[Shane McAnally]]. For this performance as Beau, he was nominated for a [[Drama Desk Awards|Drama Desk Award]].<ref name="Playbill Andrew Durand">{{cite web |title=Andrew Durand |url=https://playbill.com/person/andrew-durand |website=Playbill |access-date=17 June 2025}}</ref>

In 2024, Durand starred as [[Elmer McCurdy]] in the Off-Broadway premiere of ''[[Dead Outlaw]]'',<ref>{{cite web |url=https://people.com/andrew-durand-broadway-dead-outlaw-exclusive-interview-11715915 |title=Andrew Durand Breathes Life Into Broadway's 'Dead Outlaw' (Exclusive) |website=People |access-date=2025-10-05}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/05/31/theater/dead-outlaw-andrew-durand-tonys.html |title='Dead Outlaw' and Andrew Durand on Tony Buzz — The New York Times |website=The New York Times |date=31 May 2025 |access-date=2025-10-05}}</ref> receiving an [[Outer Critics Circle Awards|Outer Critics Circle Award]]<ref name="OCC Awards 2024">{{cite news |last1=Culwell-Block |first1=Logan |title=Stereophonic Leads 2024 Outer Critics Circle Awards, Wins Best Play; See the Full List of Winners |url=https://playbill.com/article/stereophonic-leads-2024-outer-critics-circle-awards-wins-best-play-see-the-full-list-of-winners |access-date=17 June 2025 |publisher=Playbill |date=13 May 2024}}</ref> and a [[Clarence Derwent Awards|Clarence Derwent Award]].<ref name="Actor's Equity Foundation">{{cite web |title=The Clarence Derwent Award |url=https://www.actorsequityfoundation.org/clarence-derwent-award |website=Actor's Equity Foundation |access-date=17 June 2025}}</ref> The performance also earned him Drama Desk Award<ref name="Playbill Andrew Durand" /> and [[Lucille Lortel Awards|Lucille Lortel Award]] nominations,<ref name="Lortel Awards 2024">{{cite news |last1=Culwell-Block |first1=Logan |title=Ars Nova and National Black Theatre's (Pray) Leads 2024 Lucille Lortel Awards; Read the Full List of Winners |url=https://playbill.com/article/ars-nova-and-national-black-theatres-pray-leads-2024-lucille-lortel-awards-read-the-full-list-of-winners |access-date=17 June 2025 |publisher=Playbill |date=5 May 2024}}</ref> and [[Drama League Distinguished Performance Award|Drama League Distinguished Performance]]<ref name="Playbill Andrew Durand" /> and [[Tony Awards|Tony Award]] nominations after the production transferred to Broadway.<ref name="Washington Post May 1, 2025">{{cite news |last1=Kumar |first1=Naveen |last2=Floyd |first2=Thomas |title=Tony Award nominations 2025: Full list of nominees, snubs, surprises |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/entertainment/theater/2025/05/01/tony-award-nominations-2025-list/ |access-date=17 June 2025 |newspaper=The Washington Post |date=1 May 2025}}</ref>

He then performed in a [[New York City Center]] Encores! production, playing Jim Farrell in its 2024 revival of ''[[Titanic (musical)|Titanic]]''. He also played Rick Taylor in Encores's 2025 revival of ''[[Bat Boy: The Musical]]''. Durand also appeared in the film [[Here Today (film)|''Here Today'']].<ref name="Diocese of St. Augustine">{{cite news |url=https://dosafl.com/2021/05/07/here-today/ |title=Here Today|access-date=17 June 2025 |publisher=Diocese of St. Augustine}}</ref>

'''Juliana de Souza Pereira Marins'''<ref>{{Cite web|last=Brasil|first=Mariana|url=https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/cotidiano/2025/06/autopsia-de-juliana-marins-deve-ocorrer-na-noite-desta-quarta-25-dizem-membros-do-itamaraty.shtml|title=Autópsia de Juliana Marins deve ocorrer na noite desta quarta (25), dizem membros do Itamaraty|date=25 June 2025|accessdate=25 June 2025|website=Folha de S.Paulo|lang=pt-BR}}</ref> (24 August 1998 – 24 June 2025) was a Brazilian publicist and solo traveller who was making a journey across [[Southeast Asia]]. Living in [[Niterói]], in the [[Rio de Janeiro (state)|state of Rio de Janeiro]], Marins was on an extended backpacking trip through countries such as the [[Philippines]], [[Vietnam]], [[Thailand]], and [[Indonesia]] when she went missing on 21 June 2025 during a hike on [[Mount Rinjani]], a volcano on the island of [[Lombok]], Indonesia. Her death, confirmed three days later, received widespread media coverage in both Brazil and Indonesia.

== Background ==
Mount Rinjani is Indonesia's second-highest volcano and a popular but challenging trekking destination. Ascents typically require two to four days and demand a high level of physical fitness, proper equipment and professional guidance. The region is known for its steep, narrow paths and unpredictable weather, and has been the site of other accidents involving tourists.<ref>{{Cite web |date=22 June 2025 |title=Como é a trilha para o vulcão onde brasileira caiu na Indonésia |url=https://g1.globo.com/rj/rio-de-janeiro/noticia/2025/06/22/trilha-de-mais-de-dois-dias-e-um-dos-vulcoes-mais-dificeis-de-escalar-da-indonesia-como-e-ponto-turistico-onde-brasileira-caiu.ghtml |accessdate=24 June 2025 |website=G1 |lang=pt-br}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=24 June 2025 |title=Caso Juliana Marins: por que monte Rinjani é tão perigoso e quantas mortes ocorreram? |url=https://www.bbc.com/portuguese/articles/cy4n8w78yq7o |accessdate=24 June 2025 |website=BBC News Brasil |lang=pt-br}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Juliana Marins é 10ª pessoa a morrer no Monte Rinjani, na Indonésia, nos últimos 5 anos |url=https://www.otempo.com.br/mundo/2025/6/24/juliana-marins-e-10-pessoa-a-morrer-no-monte-rinjani-na-indonesia-desde-2020 |accessdate=24 June 2025 |website=O Tempo |lang=pt-BR}}</ref>

== Disappearance ==
On 21 June 2025, Marins went missing while hiking on Mount Rinjani, an active Indonesian volcano with an elevation of 3,726 metres (12,224 ft.).  According to her family, Marins suffered from fatigue and asked to rest. She was left alone for more than an hour, and then slipped, falling about 300 metres below the main path.<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 June 2025 |title=Rinjani: Rescuers search for Brazilian tourist Juliana Marins on Indonesian volcano |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/crk60k8gp8jo |access-date=24 June 2025 |website=BBC |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nsctotal.com.br/noticias/brasileira-desaparecida-em-vulcao-na-indonesia-foi-encontrada-com-vida |title=Brasileira desaparecida em vulcão na Indonésia foi encontrada com vida |date=22 June 2025 |work=NSC Total |accessdate=24 June 2025 |lang=pt-BR }}{{Dead link|date=December 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Martins|first=Filipe|url=https://g1.globo.com/politica/noticia/2025/06/24/governo-lamenta-morte-de-brasileira-que-caiu-em-trilha-de-vulcao-na-indonesia.ghtml|title=Governo lamenta morte de brasileira na Indonésia|date=24 June 2025|accessdate=24 June 2025|website=G1|lang=pt-br}}</ref>

Later that day, drone footage captured by other hikers revealed her location on a slope below the main trail. The footage confirmed that she was alive and conscious after her initial fall.<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 June 2025 |title=Tourist Who Fell Into Volcano Was 'Abandoned' by Tour Guide |url=https://www.thedailybeast.com/juliana-marins-was-abandoned-by-tour-guide-before-falling-into-volcano/ |access-date=24 June 2025 |website=The Daily Beast |language=en}}</ref>{{citation needed|date=April 2026}} Due to the rugged terrain, dense fog and low temperatures, emergency crews were initially unable to reach her.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://sul21.com.br/noticias/2025/06/itamaraty-aciona-equipe-para-resgate-de-brasileira-em-vulcao-na-indonesia/ |title=Itamaraty aciona equipe para resgate de brasileira em vulcão na Indonésia |work=Sul21 |date=23 June 2025 |accessdate=24 June 2025 |lang=pt-br }}{{Dead link|date=December 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nsctotal.com.br/noticias/terceiro-dia-de-buscas-por-brasileira-desaparecida-na-indonesia-e-interrompido-dizem-familiares|title=Terceiro dia de buscas por brasileira desaparecida na Indonésia é interrompido, dizem familiares|accessdate=24 June 2025|website=NSC Total|lang=pt-BR}}</ref>

== Rescue operations ==
Search efforts involved Indonesian authorities at the request of the Brazilian government. Brazil's [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Brazil)|Ministry of Foreign Affairs]] confirmed that two diplomats had been sent to Indonesia to monitor the situation and provide support to Marins's family. Via drone footage, rescuers had initially established her position on 21 June at a depth of about 300 metres (984 feet), but were unable to reach her. On 22 June, Marins was no longer in her initial position. The next day, her position was identified at a depth of approximately 600 metres (1,968 feet).{{citation needed|date=April 2026}}

Drone footage captured by tourists was instrumental in pinpointing Marins's position. However, rescue teams faced significant challenges, including hazardous slopes, unpredictable weather and limited visibility. Helicopter assistance was considered but ultimately ruled out due to unsafe conditions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brazilian Tourist, 26, Trapped Deep Inside Active Volcano In Indonesia, Rescue Underway |url=https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/brazilian-tourist-26-trapped-deep-inside-active-volcano-in-indonesia-rescue-underway-8749629 |access-date=24 June 2025 |website=NDTV |language=en}}</ref>

Marins's family disputed reports that she had received aid during the days she remained stranded, stating she was without food, water or thermal protection.<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 June 2025 |title=Brazilian tourist found dead after falling from an Indonesian volcano |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/nation-world/brazilian-tourist-found-dead-after-falling-from-an-indonesian-volcano/ |access-date=24 June 2025 |website=The Seattle Times |language=en-US}}</ref>

The rescue operation was carried out by the [[National Search and Rescue Agency|Basarnas]] teams, the Lotim Brimob SAR Unit, the [[Indonesian Forest Rangers|Forest Police]], the EMHC, Lorax, local workers and the Rinjani Squad.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=Viana|first=Luana|url=https://www.metropoles.com/mundo/tv-na-indonesia-mostra-imagem-de-brasileira-morta-apaga-e-se-desculpa|title=TV na Indonésia mostra imagem de brasileira morta, apaga e se desculpa|date=24 June 2025|accessdate=26 June 2025|website=[[Metrópoles]]|lang=pt-BR}}</ref>

== Death and aftermath ==
On 24 June 2025, Indonesian rescue teams reached Marins's body, and her family confirmed via social media that she had died. Her body, affected by the extreme terrain and adverse weather conditions, was recovered after teams arrived at the location.<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 June 2025 |title=Juliana Marins: Brazilian tourist who fell off Indonesian volcano found dead |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c939q6k1ewwo |access-date=24 June 2025 |website=BBC |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Teresia |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/06/24/world/asia/brazilian-indonesia-volcano-rescue.html |access-date=24 June 2025 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web The authorities published the results of the autopsy on 27 June, where it was revealed that the cause of death was fractures in various parts of the body, along with haemorrhaging, after one fall, with forensic expert Ida Bagus Alit estimating that death occurred around 20 minutes after the trauma. No signs of hypothermia were found.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/nacional/brasil/medico-de-autopsia-diz-que-juliana-marins-morreu-20-minutos-apos-queda/|title=Médico de autópsia diz que Juliana Marins morreu 20 minutos após queda|date=27 June 2025|accessdate=27 June 2025|website=CNN Brasil|lang=pt-BR}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/portuguese/articles/cdx5ggydy2yo|title=Morte de Juliana Marins em vulcão na Indonésia: o que autópsia revela|date=27 June 2025|accessdate=27 June 2025|website=BBC News Brasil|lang=pt-br}}</ref> Mariana Marins, Juliana's sister, says that the family only found out through the media, and that the superficial information contradicts the reports and videos on the mountain.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Bustamante|first=Anna|url=https://oglobo.globo.com/rio/noticia/2025/06/27/autopsia-de-juliana-marins-familia-critica-falta-ninguem-falou-com-a-gente-ficamos-sabendo-pela-midia.ghtml|title=Pai e irmã de Juliana Marins souberam de resultado de autópsia pela imprensa: 'Ninguém falou com a gente'|date=27 June 2025|accessdate=27 June 2025|website=O Globo|lang=pt-br}}</ref> 

Marins's remains were repatriated on 1 July. She was buried in Niterói on 4 July.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Bustamante|first=Anna|url=https://apnews.com/article/brazilian-hiker-burial-indonesia-volcano-283186e07c72ebbf378e2d67b73d81da |title=Brazilian hiker buried after fatal fall from Indonesian volcano |date=4 July 2025 |accessdate=5 July 2025 |website=AP News |lang=en}}</ref> 

===Reactions===
Marins's death generated public commotion on Brazilian social networks and strong press coverage. Friends and family mobilized campaigns to press for more agility in the rescue. The Itamaraty ([[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Brazil)|Foreign Ministry]]) confirmed that it was sending two representatives to Indonesia to monitor the operation and support the family.<ref name=":0"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.metropoles.com/brasil/brasileira-desaparecida-em-vulcao-sera-resgatada-neste-domingo |title=Brasileira desaparecida em vulcão será resgatada neste domingo |work=Metrópoles |date=23 June 2025 |accessdate=24 June 2025 |lang=pt-BR }}{{Dead link|date=December 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> The Itamaraty and various members of the government have expressed their regrets.<ref name=":0" /> A group of MPs has filed a request for the Itamaraty to investigate the delay in the rescue.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Rocha|first=Valentina|url=https://veja.abril.com.br/brasil/deputados-protocolaram-pedido-junto-ao-itamaraty-para-investigar-demora-no-envio-de-ajuda-a-juliana-marins/|title=Deputados protocolaram pedido junto ao Itamaraty para investigar demora no envio de ajuda a Juliana Marins|date=24 June 2025|accessdate=25 June 2025|website=VEJA|lang=pt-BR}}</ref> Internally in Indonesia, according to ''Indonesia Business Post'', experts and advocacy groups have started to advocate, among other things, investment in advanced equipment for the rescue team, and bilateral agreements on how to deal with foreign victims in the local tourism sector.<ref>{{cite web|last=Rinaldi|first=Renold|url=https://indonesiabusinesspost.com/4607/society-environment-and-culture/brazilian-climber-s-death-at-rinjani-questions-over-indonesia-s-rescue-protocols|title=Brazilian climber's death at Rinjani questions over Indonesia's rescue protocols|date=25 June 2025|accessdate=25 June 2025|website=Indonesia Business Post}}</ref>

As an actor, he gained recognition by playing the lead role of Jung Eun-ho in the [[Boys' love]] web series ''Tinted With You''.{{cite web | title=A.C.E's Jun on playing a gay character in 'Tinted with You': "I thought about it a lot, in great detail" | website=[[NME]] | date=17 January 2022 | url=https://www.nme.com/news/tv/a-c-e-jun-playing-gay-character-tinted-with-you-thoughts-feelings-hopes-3139240 }} On September 4, 2026, he became the winner of Korea's Next Wave, the national final to choose Korea's representative in the [[Eurovision Song Contest Asia]] 2026 in [[Bangkok]], [[Thailand]].{{cite web|url=https://eurovoix.com/2026/09/04/south-korea-junhee-to-eurovision-asia/|title=🇰🇷 South Korea: Junhee to Eurovision Asia|website=Eurovoix|last=Washak|first=James|date=2026-09-04|access-date=2026-09-04}} ==Career== ===Pre-debut: Stage acting debut=== Park Junhee was a former [[CJ E&M]] and [[Jellyfish Entertainment]] trainee for seven years, and during that period he almost debuted three times. In 2016 he joined Beat Interactive. He made many covers and dance practices, posted on their official channels as well as 1MILLON channel. He made his musical debut in 2016 in ''Peste''. Park appeared on episode seven of ''[[I Can See Your Voice (South Korean game show) season 4|I Can See Your Voice 4]]'' in 2017. '''Alif Hilal''' (formerly '''Lyra Pramuk'''; born September 20, 1990) is an American singer, songwriter and performance artist.

==Early life and education==
Hilal<ref name="TQ2026">{{cite web |last1=Eede |first1=Christian |title=Lyra Pramuk Changes Name to Alif Hilal After Converting to Islam |url=https://thequietus.com/news/lyra-pramuk-changes-name-to-alif-hilal-after-converting-to-islam/ |website=[[The Quietus]] |access-date=11 June 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260611165804/https://thequietus.com/news/lyra-pramuk-changes-name-to-alif-hilal-after-converting-to-islam/ |archive-date=11 June 2026 |date=10 June 2026}}</ref> grew up in [[Hollidaysburg, Pennsylvania]].<ref name="PF2020">{{cite web|first=Eric|last=Torres|url=https://pitchfork.com/features/rising/lyra-pramuk-fountain-interview/|title=Lyra Pramuk's Surreal Songs of the Self|website=pitchfork.com|date=23 June 2020}}</ref> As a young adult, she performed on stage in church choirs, orchestras, and with musical theater groups.<ref name="PF2020" />  Hilal, who grew up as a boy, said she didn't feel the need to "come out as a gay man" because "it was dangerous to be different."<ref>{{cite web|first=Jeff|last=Spevak|url=https://www.wxxinews.org/across-the-universe/2020-08-12/lyra-pramuks-transition-in-music-and-life|title=Lyra Pramuk's transition, in music and life|website=wxxinews.org|date=12 August 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Beate|last=Scheder|url=https://taz.de/Debuetalbum-von-Lyra-Pramuk/!5675876/|title=Posthumanes Singen|website=taz.de|date=9 April 2020|language=de}}</ref>  Hilal moved to [[Rochester, New York]], where she attended the [[Eastman School of Music]] and participated in a program that required her to complete daily vocal exercises in six different languages.<ref name="PF2020" /> During her studies, she spent several periods abroad in [[Berlin]], where she made contacts with various musicians and artists and became acquainted with the city's techno scene.<ref name="PF2020" />

==Career==
After graduating from Eastman, Hilal moved to Berlin in 2013 and released her first vocal pieces via [[Bandcamp]].<ref name="PF2020" /> She collaborated with sound artists such as [[Holly Herndon]] and [[Colin Self (composer)|Colin Self]] and attended artist-in-residence programs in [[Tokyo]] and [[Stockholm]].<ref name="PF2020" /> At this time,  Hilal also publicly came out as transgender, which she documented thoroughly on her [[Instagram]] channel.<ref name="PF2020" />

In 2020, Hilal's debut studio album, ''Fountain'', was released on the Icelandic label [[Bedroom Community]]. The remix album ''Delta'' followed in 2021,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Simpson |first=Paul |title=Lyra Pramuk Songs, Albums, Reviews, Bio & More... |url=https://www.allmusic.com/artist/lyra-pramuk-mn0003840536 |access-date=6 July 2025 |website=[[AllMusic]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Cetin |first=Marissa |date=27 March 2025 |title=Lyra Pramuk announces new album, ''Hymnal'', shares 'Rewild': Listen |url=https://djmag.com/news/lyra-pramuk-announces-new-album-hymnal-shares-rewild-listen |access-date=6 July 2025 |website=[[DJ Mag]] |language=en}}</ref> featuring reworkings of her tracks by [[Valgeir Sigurðsson]], Colin Self, [[Hudson Mohawke]], [[Kara-Lis Coverdale]], [[Caterina Barbieri]], Eris Drew, [[Ben Frost]], Gabber Modus Operandi, and Tygapaw.<ref>{{cite web|first=Günseli|last=Yalcinkaya|url=https://www.dazeddigital.com/music/article/54310/1/lyra-pramuks-delta-album-takes-the-concept-of-the-remix-to-bold-extremes|title=Lyra Pramuk's Delta album takes the concept of the remix to bold extremes|website=dazeddigital.com|date=28 September 2021|access-date=29 July 2025|archive-date=28 January 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230128192651/https://www.dazeddigital.com/music/article/54310/1/lyra-pramuks-delta-album-takes-the-concept-of-the-remix-to-bold-extremes|url-status=live}}</ref> Her second studio album, ''[[Hymnal (Lyra Pramuk album)|Hymnal]]'', was released in 2025 on the German label [[!K7 Music|7k!]].<ref name="Mojo">{{Cite magazine |date=August 2025 |title=Lyra Pramuk – ''Hymnal'' review |magazine=[[Mojo (magazine)|Mojo]] |page=86 |issue=381 |issn=1351-0193}}</ref>

Hilal teaches "Experiments in the Future of Performance" at [[Campus of New York University#Foreign facilities|NYU Berlin]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://tisch.nyu.edu/special-programs/study-abroad/study-abroad-faculty/berlin-faculty/berlin-faculty--the-clive-davis-institute-x-berlin0/LyraPramuk0.html|title=Lyra Pramuk|website=tisch.nyu.edu|access-date=22 June 2025}}</ref>

On 6 June 2026 Hilal announced on Instagram that she had changed her name from Lyra Pramuk following a [[conversion to Islam]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ra.co/news/85389|title=Lyra Pramuk changes name to Alif Hilal following conversion to Islam|website=[[Resident Advisor]]|date=10 June 2026|first=Michael|last=Lawson|access-date=29 July 2026}}</ref>

'''Sean Fredrick Bell'''<ref name=jointsitting_sept2025>{{cite web|url=https://www.parliament.nsw.gov.au/Hansard/Pages/HansardFull.aspx#/DateDisplay/HANSARD-1820781676-101090/HANSARD-1820781676-101124|title=Legislative Council Hansard - 18 September 2025 – Proof - Election of a Senator|website=Parliament of New South Wales|date=18 September 2025|access-date=19 September 2025|archive-date=13 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170113051819/https://www.parliament.nsw.gov.au/Hansard/Pages/HansardFull.aspx#/DateDisplay/HANSARD-1820781676-101090/HANSARD-1820781676-101124|url-status=live}}</ref> (born 1 August 1987) is an Australian politician who sits in the [[Australian Senate|Senate]] as a member of [[Pauline Hanson's One Nation]], representing the state of [[New South Wales]]. He was appointed to the Senate on 18 September 2025, following his nomination by Pauline Hanson’s One Nation to fill a casual vacancy, which was confirmed at a joint sitting of the New South Wales [[Parliament of New South Wales|parliament]]. Bell succeeded fellow One Nation senator [[Warwick Stacey]], who resigned from the Senate on 19 August 2025 citing ill health. <ref name=SeanBellappointmentLatham>{{cite web|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2025-09-18/one-nation-queenslander-sean-bell-nsw-senator/105790262|title=Queenslander Sean Bell appointed NSW senator after parliament vote|work=ABC News|author=Pablo Viñales & Alexander Lewis|date=18 September 2025|access-date=18 September 2025|archive-date=19 September 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250919232623/https://www.abc.net.au/news/2025-09-18/one-nation-queenslander-sean-bell-nsw-senator/105790262|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Early life==
Prior to entering politics, Bell worked in retail, hospitality and warehousing before studying journalism at [[Griffith University]] and also attaining a Certificate III in Investigative Services.<ref>{{cite web |author=<!-- not stated --> |date= |title=Senator Sean Bell |url=https://www.onenation.org.au/sean-bell |website=Pauline Hanson's One Nation |location= |access-date=17 February 2026 |archive-date=22 April 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260422031056/https://www.onenation.org.au/sean-bell |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Political career==
Bell has been affiliated with One Nation and party leader [[Pauline Hanson]] for many years, having spent nine years prior to his appointment as a staffer and senior advisor to Hanson.<ref name=ONstatement>{{cite web|url=https://www.onenation.org.au/sean-bell-to-represent-nsw-for-one-nation|title=Sean Bell to represent NSW for One Nation|work=onenation.org.au|date=16 September 2025|access-date=16 September 2025|archive-date=16 September 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250916023946/https://www.onenation.org.au/sean-bell-to-represent-nsw-for-one-nation|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.news.com.au/national/politics/pauline-hanson-selects-one-nation-adviser-sean-bell-to-fit-vacant-one-nation-spot/news-story/5f9cef2a274296e7ed1bdd3287d15e7d|title=Pauline Hanson selects One Nation adviser Sean Bell to fit vacant One Nation spot|author=Jessica Wang|date=16 September 2025|work=news.com.au|access-date=16 September 2025|archive-date=16 September 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250916035520/https://www.news.com.au/national/politics/pauline-hanson-selects-one-nation-adviser-sean-bell-to-fit-vacant-one-nation-spot/news-story/5f9cef2a274296e7ed1bdd3287d15e7d|url-status=live}}</ref>

Bell has cited "ending mass migration" and abolishing [[Net-zero emissions|net-zero]] as his main political priorities.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.standard.net.au/story/9067309/incoming-one-nation-senator-vows-to-end-mass-migration/|work=The Standard|date=16 September 2025|title=Incoming One Nation senator vows to end mass migration|author=Jacob Shteyman|access-date=16 September 2025|archive-date=16 September 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250916031448/https://www.standard.net.au/story/9067309/incoming-one-nation-senator-vows-to-end-mass-migration/|url-status=live}}</ref> 

At the time of his appointment to the Senate, Bell was listed on the electoral roll as a [[Queensland]] resident. During the joint sitting to confirm his appointment, Bell's status was questioned by former One Nation state leader [[Mark Latham]], who attempted to block the nomination on the basis of what he described as an implied right to equal representation of the states under the [[Australian Constitution]].<ref name=SeanBellappointmentLatham/> Although the Constitution does not preclude a Senate candidate from living in another state or territory from the one they represent, such cases are rare. Latham's attempt was blocked by the chamber by 100 votes to 3.<ref name=jointsitting_sept2025/><ref name=SeanBellappointmentLatham/> A party spokesperson later confirmed that Bell would move from Queensland to New South Wales.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Maddison |first1=Max |title=Pauline Hanson nominated her staffer for a NSW Senate seat. He lives in Queensland |url=https://www.smh.com.au/politics/federal/pauline-hanson-nominated-her-staffer-for-a-nsw-senate-seat-he-lives-in-queensland-20250917-p5mvrx.html |access-date=18 September 2025 |work=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]] |date=18 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250918010701/https://www.smh.com.au/politics/federal/pauline-hanson-nominated-her-staffer-for-a-nsw-senate-seat-he-lives-in-queensland-20250917-p5mvrx.html |archive-date=18 September 2025 |url-status=live |url-access=limited }}</ref>

He became One Nation's Senate Whip on 27 October that year.<ref>{{Cite Au Parliament|name=Senator Sean Bell|mpid=319142|access-date=12 November 2025}}</ref>

Polunsky Unit]] }} {{more sources|date=December 2025}} '''Blaine Keith Milam''' (December 12, 1989 – September 25, 2025) was an American convicted murderer who was executed in 2025 for the 2008 murder of Amora Carson, his girlfriend's 13-month-old daughter. ==Early life== Milam was born on December 12, 1989, in [[Gregg County]], [[Texas]]. He left school after completing the fourth grade. Prior to December 2008, he moved to [[Rusk County, Texas|Rusk County]].{{Cite web |title=Blaine Milam |url=https://www.tdcj.texas.gov/death_row/dr_info/milamblaine.html |access-date=September 27, 2025 |website=Texas Department of Criminal Justice}} ==Murder of Amora Carson== On December 2, 2008, 10 days before his 19th birthday, Milam called the police to report that he had found his girlfriend's 13-month-old daughter, Amora Carson (November 12, 2007 – December 2, 2008),{{Cite web |date=September 3, 2024 |title=Teen Mom Allows Her Fiancé to Perform an Exorcism on Her Infant |url=https://theretrobliss.medium.com/teen-mom-allows-her-fianc%C3%A9-to-perform-an-exorcism-on-her-infant-f55133e25fec |access-date=2026-09-02 |website=Medium |language=en}} dead. At the time, Milam was engaged to Amora's mother, Jessica Carson, and they were living in a trailer in [[Rusk County, Texas]]. Police arrived to find Amora's body with numerous severe injuries, including multiple bite marks and broken ribs. When questioned by police, both Milam and Carson initially said they had left Amora alone for about an hour before returning to find her dead. However, they later changed their stories, claiming that Amora had become possessed by demons, and that they had attempted to perform an [[exorcism]] on her.{{Cite web |last=Myers |first=Amanda Lee |title=Double execution: Texas, Alabama execute inmates within minutes of each other |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2025/09/25/texas-alabama-executions-geoffrey-west-david-milam/86353546007/ |access-date=2025-09-27 |website=USA TODAY |language=en-US}} A subsequent autopsy indicated that Amora had been beaten, strangled, sexually mutilated, and had 24 human bitemarks covering her entire body in what the medical examiner called the worst case of brutality he had ever seen.{{Cite web | url=https://www.supremecourt.gov/DocketPDF/25/25-5712/375831/20250924182811018_Milam%20Orig.%20Writ%20FINAL.pdf | title=Respondent's brief in opposition to original petition and motion for stay of execution | website=www.supremecourt.gov}} In 2010, Milam was sentenced to death.{{Cite web |last=Noriega |first=Travis |date=September 24, 2025 |title=Rusk County man convicted of toddler's 'exorcism' death has been executed |url=https://www.kltv.com/2025/09/24/rusk-county-man-convicted-toddlers-exorcism-death-set-be-executed/ |access-date=2025-09-27 |website=KLTV |language=en}} After his conviction and death sentence, Milam continued to maintain his innocence, arguing that Carson was responsible for Amora's murder, and that she was responsible for claiming that Amora was possessed by demons. Milam's lawyers later attempted to challenge his death sentence, both on the grounds that it was based on discredited forensic [[bite mark analysis]], and that Milam himself was [[intellectually disabled]] and thus could not be constitutionally executed.{{Cite web |title=Texas man facing execution for fatally beating 13-month-old girl during 'exorcism' |url=https://abcnews.go.com/US/wireStory/texas-man-facing-execution-fatally-beating-13-month-125915097 |access-date=2025-09-27 |website=ABC News |language=en}} According to the state, it was Milam who inflicted the injuries on Amora while Carson watched and did not intervene. Carson was later sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole for her role in the crime. ==Execution== Milam's execution was stayed in 2019 and 2021{{cite news|url=https://www.kltv.com/2020/08/10/execution-date-set-man-convicted-death-east-texas-toddler/|title=Execution date set for man convicted in death of East Texas toddler|website=[[KLTV]]|access-date=September 28, 2025}}{{cite news|date=January 15, 2021|title=Appeals court stays Texas' first scheduled 2021 execution|work=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]|url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/news/article/Appeals-court-stays-Texas-first-scheduled-2021-15875298.php|access-date=September 28, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210122015942/https://www.sfchronicle.com/news/article/Appeals-court-stays-Texas-first-scheduled-2021-15875298.php|archive-date=January 22, 2021}} to permit him to appeal his conviction and sentence, but these appeals failed, and the trial court had found that Milam was not intellectually disabled. The Supreme Court denied Milam's application for a stay of his execution on his scheduled execution date, September 25, 2025. Milam was executed by [[lethal injection]] later that day, at the [[Huntsville Unit]] in [[Huntsville, Texas]]. In his final statement before his execution, he did not express remorse for his crimes and instead thanked his supporters, professed his Christian faith and expressed gratitude to the [[Texas Department of Criminal Justice]] for opening its prison chaplaincy program to death row inmates:{{Cite web |last=Runnels |first=Ayden |date=September 25, 2025 |title=Texas executes man convicted of killing 13-month-old girl in 2008 |url=https://www.texastribune.org/2025/09/25/texas-execution-blaine-milam/ |access-date=2025-09-27 |website=The Texas Tribune |language=en}} {{blockquote|"I would like to give a special thanks to all of you for showing me kindness, compassion, empathy, love and support and believing in me. Thank you for everything that y'all have done. I would also like to thank the directors of chaplaincy of TDCJ for opening up the faith based program on death row and allowed me to be accepted into it to find Jesus Christ our Lord and Savior. And if any of you would like to see me again, I implore all of you no matter who you are to accept Jesus Christ as your Lord and Savior and we will meet again. I love you all, bring me home Jesus."}} Milam was one of the two American inmates executed that day; the other being Geoffrey Todd West in [[Capital punishment in Alabama|Alabama]], who shot and killed Margaret Berry during a robbery.{{Cite news|date=2025-09-25 |title=Alabama executes man with nitrogen gas for 1997 shooting death of store clerk|url= '''Shae Cornette''' ({{nee|'''Peppler'''}}; born August 20, 1986) is an American television sports anchor who is the host of [[ESPN]]'s ''[[First Take (talk show)|First Take]]''.

==Early life==

Cornette was born and raised in [[Park Ridge, Illinois]].<ref name="I20"/> She attended [[Indiana University Bloomington]], where she developed an interest in [[sports broadcasting]], and graduated with her degree in [[broadcast journalism]].<ref name="I20"/> During college, she completed internships with [[MTV Networks]] and [[Showtime Networks]] and was a [[production assistant]] for [[CBS]] coverage of [[Chicago Bears]] games.<ref name="I20"/>

==Career==

Cornette began her career in Chicago with the [[Big Ten Network]] and ''Chicago Huddle'' on [[WLS-TV]] (ABC 7).<ref name="E">{{cite web|url=https://espnpressroom.com/us/bios/shae-peppler-cornette/|title=Shae Peppler Cornette|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=2025-10-17}}</ref> She also worked for [[Campus Insiders]] (later [[Stadium (sports network)|Stadium]]) and appeared on ''Morning Dose'' on [[WGN-TV]] (the CW).<ref name="C20"/> She spent two years with [[WFLD]] (Fox-32) as a field reporter and weekend sports anchor, most prominently as an on-site correspondent during [[Chicago Bears]] games.<ref name="C20"/> She also co-hosted [[David Kaplan (radio)|David Kaplan]]'s talk show on [[WMVP]] (ESPN 1000).<ref name="C20"/>

In March 2020, Cornette moved to Connecticut and joined her husband as the co-host of [[ESPN Radio]]'s weekly football show ''[[ESPN Radio College GameDay|GameDay]]''.<ref name="A20">{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2169785/2020/10/30/married-to-the-job-and-each-other-the-cornettes-are-a-first-on-espn-radio/|title=Married to the job and each other, the Cornettes are a first on ESPN Radio|last=Deitsch|first=Richard|date=2020-10-30|website=[[The Athletic]]|access-date=2025-10-17}}</ref> They were the first married couple to host an ESPN Radio show.<ref name="I20"/> She also became a host for [[SiriusXM]]'s ''[[SiriusXM NFL Radio|NFL Radio]]'' channel.<ref name="A20"/> In October 2021, the couple became the hosts of the relaunched daily [[ESPN+]] TV show ''[[SportsNation (TV program)|SportsNation]]''.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://awfulannouncing.com/espn/espn-sportsnation-gets-new-look-with-hosts-jordan-and-shae-cornette.html|title=ESPN's SportsNation gets a new look with hosts Jordan and Shae Cornette|date=2021-10-11|last=Casselberry|first=Ian|access-date=2025-10-17|website=Awful Announcing}}</ref> Her role at ESPN grew as she became a regular anchor for ''[[SportsCenter]]''.<ref name="L25"/> In October 2025, she was named to succeed [[Molly Qerim]] as co-host of ''[[First Take (talk show)|First Take]]'' starring [[Stephen A. Smith]].<ref name="L25">{{cite news|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/story/2025-10-16/shae-cornette-first-take-stephen-a-smith-espn-molly-qerim-sportscenter|title=Shae Cornette is named as Molly Qerim's replacement as host of ESPN's 'First Take'|last=Schilken|first=Chuck|date=2025-10-16|newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]]|access-date=2025-10-17}}</ref>

==Personal life==

Cornette met her husband, sports announcer and former [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]] basketball player Jordan Cornette, while working for [[Campus Insiders]] in 2014.<ref name="I20">{{cite news|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/2020/11/03/espn-duo-cornettes-shes-iu-grad-he-played-basketball-notre-dame/6000971002/|title=ESPN's newest duo the Cornettes: She's an IU grad, he played basketball at Notre Dame|last=Hunsinger Benbow|first=Dana|date=2020-11-03|newspaper=[[The Indianapolis Star]]|access-date=2025-10-17}}</ref> The couple married on June 1, 2019.<ref name="C20">{{cite news|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2020/01/21/sportscaster-shae-peppler-is-leaving-fox-32-and-wmvp-am-1000/|title=Sportscaster Shae Peppler is leaving Fox-32 and WMVP-AM 1000|last=Rosenthal|first=Phil|date=2020-01-20|newspaper=[[Chicago Tribune]]|access-date=2025-10-17}}</ref> She gave birth to their son, Joey (named after Jordan's late brother Joel, a former [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler]] basketball player), in April 2021.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/2022/12/12/espn-power-couple-jordan-shae-cornette-on-tragedy-love-and-life/69664587007/|title=ESPN power couple the Cornettes: Their love was born amid tragedy and loss. Then came Joey|last=Hunsinger Benbow|first=Dana|date=2022-12-12|newspaper=[[The Indianapolis Star]]|access-date=2025-10-17}}</ref> Their daughter, Saylor, was born in January 2023.<ref>{{cite Instagram|postid=CnUxxYPJhse|title=Welcome to the 🌎|user=shaepeppler|last=Peppler Cornette|first=Shae|date=2023-01-12|access-date=2025-10-17}}</ref>

As a result, he has [[cerebral palsy]], [[scoliosis]] and [[asthma]].<ref name=":O" /> He was homeschooled and enrolled in public school in the ninth grade.<ref name=":D" /> He finished KD conservatory college of film and dramatic arts in 2010.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jordan Walter Ross |url=https://www.backstage.com/u/jordan--walker-ross/ |website=Backstage |access-date=2 November 2025}}</ref>
