([[Acting (law)|Interim]]: Hilda Flor del Campo Medina) | term_start = November 5, 2025 | spouse = {{marriage|[[Carlos Manzo]]||2025|end=d}} | children = 2 | birth_name = Grecia Itzel Quiroz García | birth_date = {{Birth date and age|df=y|1990|1|16}} | birth_place = [[Uruapan]], Michoacán, Mexico | party = Independent | image = | caption = Quiroz García in 2026 | appointer = [[Congress of Michoacán]] | status = Substitute }} '''Grecia Itzel Quiroz García'''{{Family name footnote|[[Quiroz]]|[[García (surname)|García]]|lang=Spanish}} (born January 16, 1990) is a Mexican politician serving as the [[municipal president]] (mayor) of [[Uruapan]], [[Michoacán]]. She assumed office on November 5, 2025, following the assassination of her husband, [[Carlos Manzo]], who had been mayor. Quiroz was nominated by Manzo's independent political organization, the Movimiento del Sombrero, and appointed by the [[Congress of Michoacán]] to serve the remainder of the 2024 to 2027 term. Prior to becoming municipal president, Quiroz led the local [[National System for Integral Family Development|family services agency (DIF)]] in Uruapan during her husband's term as mayor. She previously worked in the federal [[Chamber of Deputies (Mexico)|Chamber of Deputies]] and was a candidate for the Michoacán Congress in the [[2024 Mexican local election|2024 state elections]]. == Early career == Quiroz was born in [[Uruapan]], Michoacán, in 1990 and holds a degree in political science.{{cite news |last1=Guerrero |first1=Cuitláhuac |title=¿Quién es Grecia Quiroz? la mujer que tomó el lugar de Carlos Manzo en Uruapan |url=https://oem.com.mx/elsoldemorelia/mexico/quien-es-grecia-quiroz-la-mujer-que-tomara-el-lugar-de-carlos-manzo-en-uruapan-26642934 |work=[[El Sol de México]] |date=2025-11-04 |language=es}}{{cite news |last1=Cabrera |first1=César |title=¿Quién es Grecia Quiroz, viuda de Carlos Manzo y la nueva alcaldesa de Uruapan? |url=https://www.milenio.com/estados/grecia-quiroz-esposa-carlos-manzo-alcaldesa-uruapan-perfil |work=[[Milenio]] |date=2025-11-04 |language=es}} As of January 2024, she worked in the [[Chamber of Deputies (Mexico)|Chamber of Deputies]].{{cite web |date=2 January 2024 |title=Carlos Manzo rechaza a partidos; remarca que irá por Uruapan por la vía independiente |trans-title=Carlos Manzo rejects political parties; says he will run for Uruapan as an independent candidate |url=https://metapolitica.news/2024/01/02/carlos-manzo-rechaza-a-partidos-remarca-que-ira-por-uruapan-por-la-via-independiente/ |access-date=2 November 2025 |website=Metapolítica |language=Es}} She was an early supporter of [[Carlos Manzo]]'s Movimiento del Sombrero. At that time, she was a candidate for the [[Congress of Michoacán]]'s 20th district (South Uruapan) in the [[2024 Mexican local election|2024 state elections]]. Quiroz led the local [[National System for Integral Family Development|family services agency (DIF)]] in Uruapan.{{Cite news |date=2025-11-05 |title=Slain mayor's widow vows to carry on his mission as she takes over his role in Michoacán |url=https://mexiconewsdaily.com/news/slain-mayors-widow-grecia-quiroz-uruapan-michoacan/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251106160917/https://mexiconewsdaily.com/news/slain-mayors-widow-grecia-quiroz-uruapan-michoacan/ |archive-date=2025-11-06 |access-date=2025-11-06 |work=Mexico News Daily |language=en-US}} == Municipal president of Uruapan == === Nomination === Quiroz's husband, [[Carlos Manzo]], was assassinated during a public [[Day of the Dead]] event in central Uruapan, leaving the municipal presidency vacant.{{Cite news |last=Jiménez |first=Elia Castillo |title=Grecia Quiroz, viuda de Carlos Manzo, será su relevo en la presidencia municipal de Uruapan |url=https://elpais.com/mexico/2025-11-04/grecia-quiroz-viuda-de-carlos-manzo-llama-a-la-manifestacion-pacifica-en-uruapan.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251106160819/https://elpais.com/mexico/2025-11-04/grecia-quiroz-viuda-de-carlos-manzo-llama-a-la-manifestacion-pacifica-en-uruapan.html |archive-date=2025-11-06 |access-date=2025-11-06 |work=El País México |language=es}} His death was presumed to be an execution by the [[Jalisco New Generation Cartel]].{{Cite news |date=November 5, 2025 |title=Grecia Quiroz es nueva alcaldesa de Uruapan: 'Vengo con el corazón destrozado' por asesinato de Carlos Manzo |url=https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/estados/2025/11/05/grecia-quiroz-da-primer-discurso-como-alcaldesa-de-uruapan-que-dijo/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251106154845/https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/estados/2025/11/05/grecia-quiroz-da-primer-discurso-como-alcaldesa-de-uruapan-que-dijo/ |archive-date=2025-11-06 |access-date=2025-11-06 |work=El Financiero |language=es}} The Movimiento del Sombrero proposed Quiroz as the new municipal president.{{Cite news |date=November 4, 2025 |title=Grecia Quiroz, the widow of Carlos Manzo, is proposed as mayor of Uruapan |url=https://theyucatantimes.com/2025/11/grecia-quiroz-the-widow-of-carlos-manzo-is-proposed-as-mayor-of-uruapan/ |access-date=2025-11-06 |work=The Yucatan Times}} Carlos Bautista Tafolla, a local representative for the movement, confirmed the nomination and described Quiroz as a "very experienced and strong woman" who had been with the movement "from the beginning." The Uruapan Cabildo (City Council) submitted the formal request to the state legislature, which expedited the process. The [[Congress of Michoacán|Michoacán Congress]] received the official request for her nomination and appointed her as the substitute mayor. The nomination received widespread political backing. Fabiola Alanís Sámano, the president of the Political Coordination Board (Jucopo) and the [[Morena (political party)|Morena]] party caucus coordinator, confirmed that Quiroz had the "absolute support" of all political forces and stated, "There will be no difficulty, no obstacle, and no one who opposes this decision." Alanís Sámano also affirmed the legislature's "unconditional support" to ensure the "governability of Uruapan". Quiroz was sworn in on Wednesday, November 5, 2025, during an [[extraordinary session]] of the state legislature to serve the remainder of the 2024 to 2027 constitutional term.{{cite news |last1=Lara |first1=Ricardo |title=Grecia Quiroz, viuda de Carlos Manzo, rinde protesta como nueva alcaldesa de Uruapan |url=https://www.excelsior.com.mx/nacional/grecia-quiroz-rinde-protesta-como-nueva-alcaldesa-de-uruapan/1749882 |access-date=2025-11-06 |work=[[Excélsior]] |date=2025-11-05 |language=es |trans-title=Grecia Quiroz, widow of Carlos Manzo, is sworn in as new mayor of Uruapan}} === Tenure === In her first speech as municipal president on November 5, 2025, Quiroz stated, "Today I come with a broken heart because they took my life partner, my partner in struggle, the father of my children." She affirmed that the {{ill|Movimiento del sombrero|es|Movimiento Independiente del Sombrero}} would not stop and that she would "take up" her husband's legacy. Quiroz criticized the government's new Michoacán Plan for Justice and Peace, lamenting that her husband had to be executed for the government to "turn its gaze to Uruapan". She asked the people of Uruapan not to falter in the fight against [[organized crime]]. She also defended her husband's legacy, stating he was "destined to be 'the [[president of Mexico]]'" and that his "hands were clean", as he "never made a pact with anyone". Amid protests following the assassination, Quiroz called for peaceful demonstrations, asking supporters to honor her husband's memory by avoiding violence or vandalism. She noted that her husband's "fight was always peaceful" and that he "always stood against violence." On Tuesday, November 4, Quiroz met with President [[Claudia Sheinbaum]] at the [[National Palace (Mexico)|National Palace]] in [[Mexico City]]. The meeting, which lasted a couple of hours, took place shortly after the presentation of a new pacification plan for Michoacán. President Sheinbaum later stated the meeting included Quiroz's brother-in-law, Juan Manzo; the federal secretary of security, [[Omar García Harfuch]]; and [[Lázaro Cárdenas Batel]], her chief of staff and a former [[governor of Michoacán]].{{cite news |title=Harfuch y Cárdenas Batel asistieron al encuentro de Sheinbaum con la viuda de Carlos Manzo |url=https://latinus.us/mexico/2025/11/5/harfuch-cardenas-batel-asistieron-al-encuentro-de-sheinbaum-con-la-viuda-de-carlos-manzo-156117.html |work=Latinus |date=2025-11-05}} According to Sheinbaum, Quiroz and her family "rightfully demand justice" and a full investigation. The president announced she would remain in communication with Quiroz to support Uruapan, where the presidency plans to open a new office. == Personal life == Quiroz was married to politician Carlos Manzo until his assassination in 2025. They had two children.{{cite web |date=1 November 2025 |title=Junto a su familia y rodeado de gente: éste fue el último video que publicó Carlos Manzo en el lugar de su asesinato |trans-title=With his family and surrounded by residents: This was the last video Carlos Manzo posted at the site where he was killed |url=https://www.milenio.com/estados/asi-fueron-los-ultimos-momentos-de-carlos-manzo-antes-de-ser-asesinado |access-date=2 November 2025 |location=Mexico City |newspaper=[[Milenio]]}} ==Notes== {{Notelist}} == References == {{reflist}} {{Authority control}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Quiroz, Grecia}} [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Place of birth missing (living people)]] [[Category:21st-century Mexican politicians]] [[Category:21st-century Mexican women politicians]] [[Category:Municipal presidents of Uruapan]] [[Category:Independent politicians in Mexico]] [[Category:1990 births]]

'''Ganavya Doraiswamy''' (born 1991), stylized professionally as '''ganavya''', is an Indian and American singer, songwriter, and musician. She has released four albums, most recently ''Nilam'' in 2025, and has collaborated with musicians including [[Quincy Jones]], [[A. R. Rahman]], and [[Esperanza Spalding]].

==Biography==
Ganavya Doraiswamy was born on July 21, 1991, in [[New York City]], United States.{{r|allmusic-bio|nyt}} When she was 7, her family moved to the town of [[Senkottai]], and then later to [[Chennai]], the capital of the [[South India]]n state of [[Tamil Nadu]].{{r|line-2024}} In India, Ganavya learned to play [[jalatharangam]] from her grandmother [[Seetha Doraiswamy]], and studied [[Carnatic music]] and [[Bharatanatyam]]. Her mother practiced the [[Pandharpur Wari]].{{r|allaboutjazz-bio|nyt}} She has one brother.

Ganavya was homeschooled for portions of her childhood instead prioritizing arts training, but later obtained undergraduate degrees in theater and psychology at [[Florida International University]] at 19.{{r|allaboutjazz-bio|line-2024}}  She then worked briefly as a rehabilitation counselor at [[Everglades Correctional Institution]] in Florida before earning a graduate degree at [[Berklee College of Music]].{{r|line-2024}} After graduating, Ganavya taught a course on South Asian music at [[Berklee Valencia]].{{r|line-2024|allmusic-bio}}

She has a graduate degree in [[Ethnomusicology]] from [[UCLA]] and a Ph.D. in Creative Practice and Critical Inquiry from [[Harvard University]], where she helped lead the Songwrights Apothecary Lab, an experimental music-based research lab founded by Spalding. Her dissertation advisors were [[Esperanza Spalding]] and [[Claire Chase]], with committee members including [[Peter Sellars]].{{r|line-2024}}{{r|nyt}}

She co-founded the We Have Voice Collective.{{r|WHV}}

==Career==
In 2015, Ganavya recorded ''Aikyam: Onnu'', a collection of [[jazz standard]]s she translated to her native language of [[Tamil language|Tamil]] and [[abhang]]s. The album was released in 2018.{{r|line-2024|allmusic-bio}}

In 2024, Ganavya released her second album ''like the sky I've been too quiet'', co-produced by [[Shabaka Hutchings]], and named after a line from a poem by [[Kaveh Akbar]].{{r|songlines-2024|ft}} Her third album ''Daughter of a Temple'' was recorded in 2022 at the [[Moores School of Music|Moores Opera House]] with over 40 featured musicians including [[Esperanza Spalding]], [[Wayne Shorter]], [[Shabaka Hutchings]], [[Immanuel Wilkins]], [[Rasika Shekar]] and [[Vijay Iyer]] and was released at the end of 2024 on Leiter.{{r|nyt}} The album is a selection of material from a week-long gathering, with initial decisions being made by Ganavya and Spalding, with the final round of mixing being led by [[Nils Frahm]] in [[Funkhaus Berlin]].{{r|songlines-2025a}} ''Daughter of a Temple'' was [[Giles Peterson]]'s Best Album of the Year, and was named by ''[[The Guardian]]'' as one of the best global albums of 2024.{{r|BBC6|guardian-2024}} Her fourth album ''Nilam'' was released in 2025, and features vocals in Tamil, [[English language|English]], and [[Old Marathi]].{{r|ft|songlines-2025b}} In 2025, a track from ''Nilam'' titled "Pasayadan" was listed as [[Barack Obama]]'s favorite tracks of the year.{{r|Obama}} ''Nilam'' was ''[[Songlines (magazine)|Songlines]]'' Album of the Year.{{r|songlines-best-of-2025}}

Ganavya has collaborated with [[Quincy Jones]], [[Nils Frahm]], [[Esperanza Spalding]], [[Immanuel Wilkins]], [[A.R. Rahman]], [[Charles Lloyd (jazz musician)|Charles Lloyd]], [[Alfredo Rodríguez (pianist, born 1985)|Alfredo Rodríguez]], [[Shabaka Hutchings]], [[Joy Harjo]], and [[Lauren Groff]]. She is a solo vocalist on multiple Grammy Award winning tracks, notably for [[Songwrights Apothecary Lab]], for which she helped create a lab by the same name at Harvard led by Spalding, and for having written and sung the first Tamil lyrics to win a [[Latin Grammy]] for [[Residente]]'s "[[Antes Que El Mundo Se Acabe]]". She has a longstanding collaborative relationship with [[Peter Sellars]], most recently having co-created an opera titled ''Nine Jewelled Deer'' with set design by [[Julie Mehretu]].{{r|allmusic-bio}}{{r|nyt}}{{r|Opera}}

'''Edgard Iván Rimaycuna Inga''' (born 24 September 1989) is a Peruvian Catholic priest and the current [[Private Secretary to the Pope|private secretary]] to [[Pope Leo XIV]].

==Biography==
[[File:Zayed Award for Human Fraternity comitee with Pope Leo 2.jpg|thumb|right|Rimaycuna seated to the right of Pope Leo during an audience in December 2025]]
Rimaycuna Inga was born on 24 September 1989 in [[Chiclayo]], Peru.<ref>{{Cite web |last=EWTN |title=Ma al fianco del Papa giorno per giorno chi c'è? I segretari particolari |url=https://www.acistampa.com/story/29853/ma-al-fianco-del-papa-giorno-per-giorno-chi-ce-i-segretari-particolari |access-date=2026-10-07 |website=ACI Stampa |language=en}}</ref> He grew up in the [[La Victoria District, Chiclayo|La Victoria district]] of Chiclayo.<ref>[https://www.diariogrupopanorama.com/gobierno-regional-de-lambayeque-rinde-homenaje-al-rvdo-edgard-ivan-rimaycuna-inga-por-su-designacion-como-secretario-del-papa-leon-xiv/ ''Gobierno Regional de Lambayeque rinde homenaje Al Rvdo. Edgard Iván Rimaycuna Inga por su designación Como Secretario del Papa León XIV''], diariogrupopanorama.com, 19 August 2025</ref> From 2001, he attended a high school in his hometown ''(Colegio Nacional San José de Chiclayo)''. After graduating, he studied philosophy and theology at the ''Santo Toribio de Mogrovejo'' seminary in Chiclayo from 2006 to 2013.<ref>José Cayetano Chávez: [https://elcomercio.pe/peru/edgard-rimaycuna-el-alumno-brillante-de-chiclayo-que-hoy-es-el-secretario-del-papa-leon-xiv-edgard-ivan-rimaycuna-inga-secretario-del-papa-chiclayo-vaticano-peru-noticia/ ''Conoce a Edgard Rimaycuna, el “alumno brillante” de Chiclayo que hoy es el secretario del Papa León XIV'']. In: ''[[El Comercio (Peru)|El Comercio]]'', 19 May 2025</ref>

During a study visit to Rome in 2006, he first met "Padre Roberto", the Rome-based Prior General of the [[Order of Saint Augustine|Augustinian Order]] (and former Prior of the Peruvian province of the Order), Robert Francis Prevost, the later pope. From 2013 to 2015, Rimaycuna Inga was parochial vicar of ''Our Lady of Guadalupe Parish'' in Chiclayo.<ref name="aleteia">{{cite web|url=https://aleteia.org/2025/05/17/who-is-fr-edgar-rimaycuna-pope-leo-xivs-trusted-aide/|title=Who is Fr. Edgar Rimaycuna, Pope Leo XIV's trusted aide?|last=Esparza|first=Daniel|publisher=Aleteia|date=2025-05-17}}</ref>  When Prevost was bishop of the [[Diocese of Chiclayo]] from 2015 to 2023, he appointed Rimaycuna Inga as parochial vicar at [[St. Mary's Cathedral, Chiclayo]]. In September 2017, he began his studies at the [[Pontifical Biblical Institute]] in Rome. After graduating a Licentiate in Scripture in 2021,<ref name="catholicherald">{{cite web|url=https://thecatholicherald.com/article/why-the-popes-secretary-has-been-made-a-monsignor-and-what-that-signifies|title=Why the Pope's secretary has been made a Monsignor|publisher=The Catholic Herald|date=2025-11-28}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.biblico.it/degrees.php|title=ACADEMIC DEGREES AWARDED IN 2020-21|publisher=Pontifical Biblical Institute}}</ref> Rimaycuna Inga went to Manesseno, a district of [[Sant’Olcese]] in Liguria, Italy, as parish vicar.<ref>[https://www.open.online/2025/05/10/papa-leone-xiv-prevost-segretario-particolare-chi-e-edgard-ivan-rimaycuna-inga/ Edgard Iván Rimaycuna Inga, chi è l’uomo-ombra di Prevost dal Perù a Roma: sarà segretario particolare di Papa Leone XIV], 10 May 2025</ref>

After Prevost moved back to Rome in 2023, as a cardinal of the [[Roman Curia]], he appointed Rimaycuna Inga as his secretary in the [[Dicastery for Bishops]] in 2024. Following Prevost's election as Pope Leo XIV on 8 May 2025, Rimaycuna Inga became [[papal private secretary]] on 11 May 2025.<ref>[https://peru21.pe/mundo/peru-es-clave-secretario-del-papa-leon-xiv-sera-un-joven-de-chiclayo/ ¡Perú es clave! Secretario del papa León XIV será un joven de Chiclayo], peru21.pe, May 11, 2025</ref> Papal private secretaries hold a position that is subordinate in protocol, but in practice often quite influential. In December 2025, Rimaycuna Inga was made [[Chaplain of His Holiness]], and therefore granted the title ''[[Monsignor]]'', as an expression of his work with the Pope Leo.<ref name="catholicherald" />

His current co-driver is [[County Donegal]] native, [[Shane Byrne (co-driver)|Shane Byrne]], who he started working with in 2025.{{Cite web |title=Jon Armstrong |url=https://www.wrc.com/en/drivers/jon-armstrong |access-date=2026-05-26 |website=Home {{!}} WRC.com® {{!}} FIA World Rally Championship {{!}} Official Website |language=en}} This change in co-drivers was due to Eoin Treacy leaving Armstrong, for his future M-Sport Ford teammate, [[Josh McErlean]]. ==Biography== [[File:Rally Poland 2021 Jon Armstrong 01.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Armstrong driving a [[Ford Fiesta Rally3]] at the [[Rally Poland]].]] Armstrong was born in [[County Fermanagh]]. the rise of the WRC's new underdog |work=[[BBC]] |date=21 January 2026}} {{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DKgmiOUN6vU?si=Lv6LF-woYnJy7Kfp |title = I Rolled on my First Ever Rally... |work=[[YouTube]] |date=9 February 2026}} {{clear left}} ==Rally results== ===WRC results=== {|class="wikitable" style="text-align:center; font-size:85%;" ! '''Kim Min-gee''' ({{Korean|hangul=김민지}}; born April 5, 1996) is a South Korean track and field athlete and media personality. Specializing in the 400-meter sprint and 400-meter hurdles, she earned the nicknames "[[Karina (South Korean singer)|Karina]] of Track and Field" and the "track and field goddess". Since 2023, she has successfully transitioned into broadcasting, appearing on popular variety programs such as ''[[Kick a Goal]]'' and ''[[Single's Inferno]] 5''.<ref name="MK_2024">{{cite web |title=“힘들어도 아직 뛰는게 좋다”…육상여신 김민지, 폭우 속 경기 출전 모습 화제 |website=Maeil Business Newspaper (매일경제) |date=18 September 2024 |url=https://www.mk.co.kr/news/society/11119005 }}</ref><ref name="WD_2022">{{cite web |title=육상 선수 김민지 “운동, 방송 활동 다 포기하지 않을 거예요” |website=Woman Dong-A (여성동아) |date=8 December 2022 |url=https://woman.donga.com/people/article/all/12/3791926/1 }}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Kim was born on April 5, 1996, in Goesan County, [[North Chungcheong Province]], South Korea. She is the middle child of four siblings (two older sisters and one younger brother). She began her athletic career in the first year of middle school at the recommendation of her physical education teacher. She graduated from Chungbuk Sports High School and later attended [[Changwon National University]], where she earned a bachelor's degree in physical education. She subsequently completed a master's degree in physical education at Inha University's Graduate School of Education.<ref name="sig">{{cite news |title=Who is Kim Min-ji? Single's Inferno season 5's viral star dubbed the 'track world's Karina' dominates Netflix |url=https://poprant.indiatimes.com/asian-dramas-kpop/who-is-kim-min-ji-singles-inferno-season-5s-viral-star-dubbed-the-track-worlds-karina-dominates-netflix-679496.html |work=PopRant |date=21 January 2026 |language=en-IN}}</ref><ref name="HCN_2022">{{cite web |title='육상계 아이돌' 김민지…“전국체전 400m 챔피언은 나” |website=kt HCN 충북방송 |date=2 September 2022 |url=https://ccn.hcn.co.kr/user/news/BD_newsView.do?news_category=05&soCode=114&socttSeq=0&socttSn=NS2022090200093&story_id=NS2022090200093&story_seq=0 }}</ref>

==Athletic career==
Kim competed primarily in the 400m and 400m hurdles. Her first major breakthrough occurred in 2014 when she won the 400-meter hurdles at the 43rd Spring National Middle and High School Athletics Championships. During her collegiate years, she was a dominant force, winning the 400m title at the National Sports Festival four times (2014, 2017, 2018 and 2019).<ref name="sig"/>

In 2018, she also won the 400 metres at the 73rd National University Athletics Championships and the 72nd National Inter-University Track and Field Championships, and placed first in the 400 metres hurdles at the 47th National Individual Athletics Championships.<ref name="Thai">{{cite news |title=Meet Kim Min-ji: The Charming Sprinter from Singles Inferno 5, Known as the Karina of Athletics |url=https://en.thairath.co.th/sport/others/2910197 |work=Thairath |date=26 January 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

In 2020, despite a reduced competition schedule due to the COVID-19 pandemic, she remained active in domestic events. She finished second in the 400 metres at the 49th National Individual Athletics Championships, and was part of the gold-medal-winning 4 × 400 metres mixed relay team at the 48th KBS Cup National Athletics Championships.<ref name="dam">{{cite news |title=진천군 떠난 '육상 카리나' 김민지, 올해 1월 화성시청에 '새 둥지' |url=https://v.daum.net/v/VmXjZef55u |work=Daum |date=January 31, 2024}}</ref>

She has also participated in football- and baseball-related activities. In 2022, she threw a ceremonial first pitch at a KBO League game between the Hanwha Eagles and the NC Dinos in Daejeon.<ref name="Thai"/>

Kim represented Jincheon County from 2019 to 2023 before joining Hwaseong City Hall in 2024 on a two-year contract. Her later career has been affected by an Achilles tendon injury sustained in late 2023.<ref name="dam"/> During her first season with Hwaseong City Hall in 2024, Kim was eliminated in the heats of the women’s 400 metres at the KTFL National Corporate Track and Field Championships. Later that year, she was appointed as a public relations ambassador and social contribution ambassador for Hwaseong City.<ref>{{cite news |title='육상 카리나' 김민지, 내년에도 화성시청에서 뛴다! |url=https://www.mhnse.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=356111 |work=엠에이치앤 |date=10 December 2024}}</ref>

==Entertainment career==

Kim became widely known in July 2022 after a video of her competing at a national athletics event without her usual goggles spread online. In October 2022, she signed an exclusive management contract with Bonboo Entertainment, which manages athletes and sports personalities.<ref name="aaa">{{cite news |last1=Pattnaik |first1=Ananya |title=Who Is Kim Min-gee? Single’s Inferno Season 5 Star Dubbed the ‘Track World’s Karina’ Takes Netflix by Storm |url=https://pragativadi.com/who-is-kim-min-gee-singles-inferno-season-5-star-dubbed-the-track-worlds-karina-takes-netflix-by-storm/#:~:text=Min%2Dji%20later%20dominated%20the,TV%20Career%20Before%20Single's%20Inferno |work=[[Pragativadi]] |date=24 January 2026}}</ref>

She later began appearing regularly on South Korean television. In 2023, she joined the [[Seoul Broadcasting System|SBS]] sports-variety program ''[[Kick a Goal]]'' as a member of FC National Family, where she played as a sprinter-type player. She also appeared in multiple seasons of ''[[Kick a Goal]]'' (seasons 4–6), participated in both editions of the ''SBS Cup'', and made guest appearances on ''[[Knowing Bros]]'' and ''[[King of Masked Singer]]''.<ref name="aaa"/>

In 2024, Kim appeared as a contestant on [[TV Chosun]]'s physical competition program ''[[King of Survival: Tribal War]]''.<ref name="aaa"/>

In late 2025, she joined [[Channel A (TV channel)|Channel A]]'s baseball variety program ''Baseball Queen''.<ref>{{cite news |title=Sports reality shows find new life through competitive realism - The Korea Times |url=https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/entertainment/shows-dramas/20251127/sports-reality-shows-find-new-life-through-competitive-realism |work=www.koreatimes.co.kr |date=27 November 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

In January 2026, she participated in the fifth season of the reality dating show ''[[Single's Inferno]]'', which led to increased public recognition.<ref>{{cite news |title=Meet The Cast Of ‘Single’s Inferno’ Season 5 |url=https://www.harpersbazaar.com.sg/lifestyle/singles-inferno-5-cast |work=Harper's Bazaar Singapore |date=21 January 2026 |language=en-SG}}</ref>

'''Alejandro "Àlex" Cano Jiménez''' (born 7 March 1988) is a Spanish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[centre-back]] for [[CE Europa]], which he [[Captain (association football)|captains]]. He is also the highest appearance-maker of the club's history.

==Club career==
[[File:CE Europa - UE Sant Andreu (49333850683) - Àlex Cano.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Cano playing for [[CE Europa|Europa]] in 2020]]
Born in [[Barcelona]], [[Catalonia]], Cano played for [[FC Barcelona]], [[CE L'Hospitalet]] and [[UE Cornellà]] as a youth, making his senior debut with the latter in 2007, in [[Primera Catalana]]. In January 2008, he moved to [[CD Marianao Poblet]], before signing for [[CE Europa]] in July 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.elpuntavui.cat/article/110749-els-germans-alex-i-carles-cano-es-van-enfrontar-per-primer-cop-diumenge-passat-en-leuropa-cornella.html|title=Els germans Àlex i Carles Cano es van enfrontar per primer cop diumenge passat en l'Europa-Cornellà|trans-title=The brothers Àlex and Carles Cano faced each other for the first time last Sunday at Europa-Cornellà|publisher=[[El Punt Avui]]|language=ca|date=2 December 2009|accessdate=27 January 2026}}</ref>

At Europa, Cano subsequently became a first-choice, and was appointed [[Captain (association football)|team captain]] in October 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://beteve.cat/esports/alex-cano-pren-el-relleu-de-delmas/|title=Àlex Cano pren el relleu de Delmàs|trans-title=Àlex Cano takes over from Delmàs|publisher=Betevé|language=ca|date=15 October 2013|accessdate=27 January 2026}}</ref> He helped the club to win the [[Copa Catalunya]] in 2015, and reached 400 matches for them on 7 February 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://beteve.cat/esports/alex-cano-arriba-400-partits-europa/|title=Àlex Cano arriba als 400 partits amb l’Europa|trans-title=Àlex Cano reaches 400 matches with Europa|publisher=Betevé|language=ca|date=7 February 2022|accessdate=27 January 2026}}</ref>

On 13 March 2022, Cano reached 403 matches with the shirt of the ''Escapulats'', becoming their highest-ever appearance maker.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://beteve.cat/esports/alex-cano-jugador-mes-partits-historia-ce-europa/|title=Àlex Cano, el jugador amb més partits de la història del CE Europa|trans-title=Àlex Cano, the player with the most matches of CE Europa's history|publisher=Betevé|language=ca|date=13 March 2022|accessdate=27 January 2026}}</ref> On 17 March 2025, he reached 500 official matches with the club,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ghrv.cat/alex-cano-fa-historia-sumant-500-partits-oficials-amb-leuropa/|title=Àlex Cano fa història sumant 500 partits oficials amb l’Europa|trans-title=Àlex Cano makes history reaching 500 official matches with Europa|publisher=Grup d'Historia Ramon Vergés|language=ca|date=17 March 2025|accessdate=27 January 2026}}</ref> and finished [[2024–25 Segunda Federación|the season]] with eight goals in 30 appearances overall as the club achieved promotion to [[Primera Federación]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://beteve.cat/esports/emocio-alex-cano-ascens-europa-1a-rfef/|title=L’emoció d’Àlex Cano després d’aconseguir l’ascens directe a la Primera RFEF|trans-title=The emotion of Àlex Cano after achieving direct promotion to ''Primera RFEF''|publisher=Betevé|language=ca|date=27 April 2025|accessdate=27 January 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
On 14 November 2025, Cano and his brother were called up to the [[Catalonia national football team|Catalonia national team]] for a friendly against [[Palestine national football team|Palestine]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://beteve.cat/esports/alex-jordi-cano-europa-albertito-sant-andreu-convocats-catalunya/|title=Àlex i Jordi Cano i Albertito, convocats amb Catalunya|trans-title=Àlex and Jordi Cano and Albertito, called up with Catalonia|publisher=Betevé|language=ca|date=14 November 2025|accessdate=27 January 2026}}</ref> He made his international debut four days later, playing the entire second half in the 2–1 win at the [[Estadi Olímpic Lluís Companys]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ghrv.cat/alex-cano-jordi-cano-i-arnau-campeny-fan-historia-amb-catalunya/|title=Àlex Cano, Jordi Cano i Arnau Campeny fan història amb Catalunya|trans-title=Àlex Cano, Jordi Cano and Arnau Campeny make history with Catalonia|publisher=Grupo d'Historia Ramon Vergés|language=ca|date=19 November 2025|accessdate=27 January 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Cano comes from a family of footballers: his younger brothers [[Carlos Cano Jiménez|Carlos]] and [[Jordi Cano|Jordi]] are also footballers, with the former being a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] and the latter being a [[Midfielder#Winger|winger]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://futbolcatalunya.com/la-familia-cano-guanya-al-nou-sardenya/|title=La família Cano guanya al Nou Sardenya|trans-title=The Cano family wins at Nou Sardenya|publisher=Futbol Catalunya|language=ca|date=14 September 2017|accessdate=27 January 2026}}</ref> Àlex and Jordi play together at Europa, and Àlex faced both his brothers (at the time at Prat) in September 2017, in a match where all three brothers scored.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.abc.es/deportes/futbol/abci-curiosa-noche-familia-cano-europa-prat-201709140828_noticia.html|title=La curiosa noche de la familia Cano en el Europa-Prat|trans-title=The curious night of the Cano family at Europa-Prat|publisher=[[ABC (newspaper)|ABC]]|language=es|date=14 September 2017|accessdate=27 January 2026}}</ref>

2017 | url=https://vindyarchives.com/news/2017/mar/12/poullas-ends-prep-career-with--wins/ | access-date=March 7, 2026}} In his four years at Canfield, Poullas amassed an overall record of 176–15. == College career == He committed to wrestling collegiality for [[Cleveland State University]] on December 2, 2016. Cleveland State was chosen after [[Ohio State University]] invited Poullas for a visit, but never made a formal offer.{{cite web | last=Simon | first=Joe | title=Canfield wrestler likes fit with CSU | website=[[Tribune Chronicle]] | date=February 15, 2017 | url=https://www.tribtoday.com/sports/high-school-sports/2017/02/canfield-wrestler-likes-fit-with-csu/ | access-date=March 5, 2026}} Poullas later transferred to [[Rider University]] in 2019.{{cite web | title=Wrestling Announces 2019-20 Recruiting Class | website=[[Rider University]] | date=August 12, 2019 | url=https://gobroncs.com/news/2019/8/12/wrestling-announces-2019-20-recruiting-class | access-date=March 5, 2026}} Following college, Poullas returned home to coach his younger brother Niko, who wrestled at [[Canfield High School]].{{cite web | last=Hiner | first=Dan | title=Poullas finds new avenue to continue wrestling | website=[[Tribune Chronicle]] | date=February 17, 2026 | url=https://www.tribtoday.com/sports/local-sports/2026/02/poullas-finds-new-avenue-to-continue-wrestling/ | access-date=March 5, 2026}} ==Takedown challenge== Poullas became a [[social media influencer]], uploading videos of people attempting to perform a [[takedown (grappling)|takedown]] on him to win $1,000.{{cite web | title=Social media sensation vows to score multiple takedowns on Arman Tsarukyan | website=[[Sherdog]] | date=February 24, 2026 | last=Nag | first=Sayan | url=https://www.sherdog.com/news/news/Social-media-sensation-vows-to-score-multiple-takedowns-on-Arman-Tsarukyan-200237 | access-date=March 5, 2026}} He maintains that no one has ever taken him down, after online video surfaced to dispute his claim. {{Short description|Uruguayan drug lord (born 1991)}} {{Use dmy dates|date=February 2026}} {{Infobox criminal | name = Sebastián Marset | image = | caption = | birth_name = Sebastián Enrique Marset Cabrera | birth_date = {{birth date and age|df=yes|1991|04|10}} | birth_place = [[Montevideo]], Uruguay | death_date = | death_place = | death_cause = | other_names = Luis Paulo Amorim Santos,
Gabriel de Souza Beumer | years_active = | occupation = [[drug trafficker]], [[businessman]], former [[association football|footballer]] | convictions = Bolivia and Paraguay: [[Illegal drug trade|drug trafficking]]; United States: [[money laundering]] | organization = | predecessor = | criminal_status = | spouse = Gianina García Troche | children = 4 | relatives = | footnotes = }} '''Sebastián Enrique Marset Cabrera''' (born 10 April 1991) is a former Uruguayan [[drug lord]] accused by authorities in several countries of leading an international cocaine trafficking and money laundering network known as the Primer Cartel Uruguayo (PCU). Considered one of the most wanted criminals in the [[Southern Cone]] for years, he was believed to have had links to groups such as the Insfrán Clan of Paraguay, the [[Primeiro Comando da Capital]] (PCC) of Brazil, and the Italian [['Ndrangheta]]. He was captured on 13 March 2026, in [[Santa Cruz de la Sierra]], Bolivia, during a major police operation and immediately extradited to the United States by [[DEA]] agents to face federal charges.{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/mundo/articles/c99jd727dgeo |title=Capturan en Bolivia al uruguayo Sebastián Marset, uno de los narcos más buscados del mundo, y lo extraditan a EE.UU. |date=13 March 2026 |publisher=BBC News Mundo |language=es}}{{cite web |url=https://cnnespanol.cnn.com/2026/03/13/latinoamerica/capturan-sebastian-marset-bolivia-uruguay-orix |title=Capturan en Bolivia al supuesto narcotraficante uruguayo Sebastián Marset, uno de los fugitivos más buscados de la DEA |date=13 March 2026 |publisher=CNN en Español |language=es}}{{cite web|url=https://www.dea.gov/documents/2026/2026-03/2026-03-14/administrator-coles-statement-capture-sebastian-marset|title=Administrator Cole's Statement on the Capture of Sebastian Marset|author=DEA Administrator|publisher=DEA|date=14 March 2026|accessdate=14 March 2026}}{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/mar/13/uruguayan-drug-trafficking-suspect-sebastian-marset-arrested-bolivia|title=Bolivia arrests alleged drug kingpin accused of putting hit on Paraguayan prosecutor|first=Thomas|last=Graham|publisher=The Guardian|date=13 March 2026|accessdate=14 March 2026}} ==Early life== Marset was born in [[Montevideo]] and grew up in the [[Piedras Blancas, Montevideo|Piedras Blancas]] neighborhood. His first links to drug trafficking date back to 2012, when he received an air shipment of hundreds of kilograms of marijuana from Paraguay, sent by Juan Domingo Viveros Cartes, uncle of former Paraguayan President [[Horacio Cartes]].{{cite web |url=https://insightcrime.org/paraguay-organized-crime-news/sebastian-marset|title=Sebastián Marset |date=22 May 2025|publisher=InSight Crime |language=es}} In 2013, he was arrested in Uruguay for another drug shipment, confessed his involvement, and was convicted. He served his sentence at the Libertad Penitentiary until his release in 2018. During his incarceration, he established key contacts with members of the Brazilian PCC and other transnational networks. ==Rise and international expansion== After his release from prison, Marset settled in Paraguay, where he created shell companies such as Total Cars to launder money. Between 2018 and 2022, he consolidated the PCU, a logistical structure that coordinated massive shipments of cocaine from Bolivia and Paraguay to European ports (mainly Belgium, the Netherlands, and Portugal). The network handled tons per operation and generated tens of millions of dollars.{{cite web |url=https://www.state.gov/sebastian-marset |title=Sebastian Enrique Marset Cabrera |date=21 May 2025 |publisher=Departamento de Estado de los Estados Unidos}} He used multiple false identities and passports from different countries. In 2021, he was arrested in Dubai with a fake [[Paraguayan passport]]. While in detention, he applied for and obtained a [[Uruguayan passport]] issued in accordance with the regulations in force at the time.{{Cite web |title=Caso narco Marset: embajada de Uruguay en Emiratos sugirió tomarse más tiempo para evaluar el pasaporte, pero el trámite siguió igual |url=https://www.elobservador.com.uy/nota/caso-narco-marset-embajada-de-uruguay-en-emiratos-sugirio-tomarse-mas-tiempo-para-evaluar-el-pasaporte-pero-el-tramite-siguio-igual-2022816111351 |access-date=2026-03-15 |website=El Observador |language=es-UY}} The episode triggered a political scandal in Uruguay, which led to the resignations of several high-ranking officials and the subsequent modification of the regulations that had allowed the procedure.{{Cite web|url=https://apnews.com/article/bustillo-marset-passport-uruguay-94a90a6eb0a0669462e7758c96924c83 |title=Uruguay's foreign minister resigns following leak of audios related to a passport scandal |date=2 November 2023 |last=Politi |first=Dante |work=Associated Press}}{{Cite web |title=Tras caso Marset, gobierno modificó decreto de emisión de pasaportes |url=https://www.elobservador.com.uy/nota/tras-caso-marset-gobierno-modifico-decreto-de-emision-de-pasaportes-202291135747 |access-date=2026-03-15 |website=El Observador |language=es-UY}} He maintained a public facade: he registered as a footballer for [[Deportivo Capiatá]] (Paraguay) and Leones de El Torno (Bolivia), where he managed the club, and presented himself as a music entrepreneur and event promoter. ==Accusations and connections== Marset is accused of being the mastermind behind the murder of Paraguayan prosecutor [[Marcelo Pecci]], which occurred on 10 May 2022, in [[Cartagena, Colombia]], during his honeymoon. He was implicated in Operation A Ultranza PY (Paraguay, 2022), which dismantled part of his network and linked the PCU to seizures of more than 16 tons of cocaine in Europe. In May 2025, the [[United States Department of Justice|U.S. Department of Justice]] indicted him for conspiracy to launder money through the U.S. financial system. The DEA listed him among its most wanted fugitives, and the State Department offered a reward of up to US$2 million. ==Fugitive and failed operations== In 2022, Marset began hiding primarily in Santa Cruz de la Sierra, Bolivia, living in a mansion in the El Urubó area with his wife, Gianina García Troche, and their children. In July 2023, a Bolivian raid seized weapons, luxury vehicles, and exotic animals, but Marset escaped. His wife was arrested in Spain in 2024 and extradited to Paraguay for money laundering. In July 2025, close Marset associated Federico Ezequiel Santoro Vassallo would sentenced to 15 years in prison by a U.S. court after pleading guilty to money laundering. ==Capture and extradition to the United States== On 13 March 2026, in a major operation by the Special Force for the Fight Against Drug Trafficking (FELCN) and the Bolivian UTOP in the Las Palmas neighborhood of Santa Cruz, Marset was captured along with four other people (two Venezuelans, a Colombian, and a relative named Tatiana Marset Alba).{{cite web|url=https://larazon.bo/nacional/2026/03/13/tatiana-marset-alba-es-la-mujer-aprehendida-tras-la-captura-del-narco-uruguayo/|title=Tatiana Marset Alba es la mujer detenida tras la captura del narco uruguayo|website=larazon.bo|language=es}} The operation, coordinated with international intelligence and the DEA, began in the early morning without incident. Hours later, he departed Bolivia by DEA plane and began his extradition to the United States (with a stopover in Lima, Peru) to face charges of money laundering and drug trafficking.{{cite web |url=https://www.infobae.com/america/america-latina/2026/03/13/el-narco-sebastian-marset-fue-detenido-en-un-operativo-policial-en-santa-cruz-de-la-sierra |title=El narco Sebastián Marset fue detenido en un operativo policial en Santa Cruz de la Sierra |date=13 March 2026 |publisher=Infobae |language=es}}{{cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/uruguayan-alleged-cartel-leader-marset-arrested-bolivia-2026-03-13/|title=Bolivia arrests accused drug kingpin Marset, transfers him to US|publisher=Reuters|date=13 March 2026|accessdate=14 March 2026}} Bolivian President [[Rodrigo Paz]] described the arrest as a "historic event" and a "turning point" in the fight against organized crime.{{cite web|url=https://abi.bo/estados-unidos-destaca-liderazgo-de-rodrigo-paz-tras-captura-de-marset/|title=Estados Unidos destaca liderazgo de Rodrigo Paz tras captura de Marset|website=abi.bo|language=es}} On 14 March 2026, DEA Administrator Terrance Cole confirmed the arrest of Marset, but noted that it was actually "today" when "DEA agents escorted Marset to the United States." On March 16, 2026, Marset would make his first court appearance since being handed over to American authorities at a federal district court in Virginia.{{cite news|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/narco-trafficker-us-court-sebastian-marset-fugitive/|title=Alleged drug lord accused of laundering money through soccer teams appears in U.S. court after years on the run|publisher=CBS News|date=March 17, 2026|accessdate=March 17, 2026}} The same day, Bolivians announced the seizure of some $15 million in assets belonging to Marset, including 16 planes, five houses and firearms. == See also == * [[Arrest of Roger Mariaca]] ==References== {{reflist}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Marset, Sebastian}} [[Category:1991 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:People from Montevideo]] [[Category:Uruguayan criminals]] [[Category:Crime bosses]] [[Category:Drug traffickers]] [[Category:People extradited from Bolivia]] [[Category:People extradited to the United States]]

'''John Martin''' (born August 3, 1998), known professionally as '''Jack Martin''', is an American actor and comedian. He is best known for ''[[La Brea (TV series)|La Brea]]'' (2021–2024) and ''[[Pizza Movie]]'' (2026).<ref name="labreaeoin">{{cite web |last=Petski |first=Denise |title='La Brea': Eoin Macken To Star, Jon Seda To Return As NBC Series Also Casts Jack Martin & Lily Santiago |url=https://deadline.com/2021/03/la-brea-eoin-macken-jon-seda-jack-martin-lily-santiago-nbc-drama-1234706752/ |website=Deadline |date=March 2021 |access-date=April 8, 2026 |archive-date=July 25, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220725222341/https://deadline.com/2021/03/la-brea-eoin-macken-jon-seda-jack-martin-lily-santiago-nbc-drama-1234706752/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Petski |first=Denise |title=Jack Martin Latest To Join Hulu's BriTANicK Comedy |url=https://deadline.com/2025/06/jack-martin-joins-britanick-comedy-hulu-1236435196/ |website=Deadline |date=June 2025 |access-date=April 8, 2026 |archive-date=April 23, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260423172956/https://deadline.com/2025/06/jack-martin-joins-britanick-comedy-hulu-1236435196/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="mindykalingseries">{{cite web |last=Petski |first=Denise |title=Mindy Kaling Series 'Not Suitable for Work' Sets Lead Cast |url=https://deadline.com/2025/08/mindy-kaling-hulu-series-not-suitable-for-work-cast-1236500174/ |website=Deadline |date=August 2025 |access-date=April 8, 2026 |archive-date=April 21, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260421091051/https://deadline.com/2025/08/mindy-kaling-hulu-series-not-suitable-for-work-cast-1236500174/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=":0" />

== Early life and education ==
Martin was born in [[Columbia, Maryland]], and raised in [[McLean, Virginia]] where he attended [[Potomac School (McLean, Virginia)|Potomac School]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2025-01-24 |title=Lili Reinhart Gives Boyfriend Jack Martin a Sweet Shoutout for Supporting Her Amid Interstitial Cystitis Diagnosis |url=https://www.cosmopolitan.com/entertainment/celebs/a60925346/who-is-jack-martin-lili-reinhart-boyfriend-facts/ |access-date=2026-04-28 |website=Cosmopolitan |language=en-US |archive-date=April 30, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260430140054/https://www.cosmopolitan.com/entertainment/celebs/a60925346/who-is-jack-martin-lili-reinhart-boyfriend-facts/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He studied political science at [[Georgetown University]], hoping to pursue a career in politics, but changed his mind after the first semester. He graduated a year early in December 2019. While at college, Martin attended summer courses in screen acting at the [[USC School of Cinematic Arts|University of Southern California School of Cinematic Arts]] and [[New York University Tisch School of the Arts]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-10-21 |title=Jack Martin |url=https://bellomag.com/ux-portfolio/jack-martin/ |access-date=2026-04-28 |website=BELLO Mag |language=en-US |archive-date=April 29, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260429124200/https://bellomag.com/ux-portfolio/jack-martin/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite news |title=Who Is Lili Reinhart's Boyfriend? All About Jack Martin |url=https://people.com/tv/who-is-jack-martin-lili-reinhart/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241226062827/https://people.com/tv/who-is-jack-martin-lili-reinhart/ |archive-date=December 26, 2024 |access-date=2026-04-28 |work=People.com |language=en |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-04-13 |title=Who Is Jack Martin? == Career ==

Martin began his career creating comedic content on social media platforms, gaining a following on [[TikTok]] prior to transitioning into television acting.<ref>{{cite web |title=La Brea Star Jack Martin Talks Leaping From Social Media to Television |url=https://comicbook.com/tv-shows/news/la-brea-jack-martin-tik-tok/ |website=ComicBook.com |access-date=April 8, 2026 |archive-date=April 9, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260409171605/https://comicbook.com/tv-shows/news/la-brea-jack-martin-tik-tok/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2021, Martin was cast as Josh Harris in the NBC science fiction drama ''[[La Brea (TV series)|La Brea]]'', appearing as a series regular throughout the show's run.<ref name="labreaeoin" /> The series achieved a wide audience across broadcast and streaming platforms.<ref>{{cite web |title=The Sci-Fi Series Everyone Forgot Has Quietly Become a 35.6 Million-Hour Streaming Obsession |url=https://collider.com/la-brea-nbc-sci-fi-series-streaming/ |website=Collider |access-date=April 8, 2026 |archive-date=April 11, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260411102400/https://collider.com/la-brea-nbc-sci-fi-series-streaming/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Following ''La Brea'', Martin joined the cast of the Hulu comedy film ''[[Pizza Movie]]'', produced by [[BriTANicK]].<ref>{{cite web |title=BriTANicK's 'Pizza Movie' Sets Hulu Premiere Date |url=https://deadline.com/2026/03/pizza-movie-streaming-premiere-date-hulu-1236743964/ |website=Deadline |date=March 2026 |access-date=April 8, 2026 |archive-date=March 4, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260304193706/https://deadline.com/2026/03/pizza-movie-streaming-premiere-date-hulu-1236743964/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He appeared in the Hulu series ''[[Not Suitable for Work]]'', created by [[Mindy Kaling]].<ref name="mindykalingseries" />

Martin has appeared in additional television and digital projects including ''[[The Rookie (TV series)|The Rookie]]'' and ''[[All Rise (TV series)|All Rise]]''.

== Personal life ==
Martin has been in a relationship with actress [[Lili Reinhart]] since 2023.<ref name=":2" /> He lives in Los Angeles, California. Martin was diagnosed with [[obsessive–compulsive disorder]], a chronic [[neuropsychiatric condition]], "late in high school,"<ref>{{cite podcast |date=July 2, 2026 |title=Jack Martin Returns|url=https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/so-true-with-caleb-hearon/id1731076727?i=1000775124206 |series=So True with Caleb Hearon |language=en | host=[[Caleb Hearon]]|time=23:19 |url-status=live |access-date=July 2, 2026|publisher=Wave}}</ref> which he remained in treatment for {{as of|2026|7|lc=y}}.

estudante executada no Rio |url=https://ponte.org/matheusa-passareli-e-revolucao-e-amor-diz-amiga-de-estudante-executada-no-rio/ |access-date=September 2, 2026 |website=Ponte Jornalismo |language=pt-BR|trans-title='Matheusa Passareli is revolution and love,' says friend of student executed in Rio}}</ref> where they created art and engaged in LGBTQ+ activism.<ref name="trans morta no Rio"/><ref>{{Cite journal |title=Os corpos e seus mundos: da poética ao ensino |url=https://lume.ufrgs.br/bitstream/handle/10183/267686/001187689.pdf?sequence=1 |journal=Lume|via=|last=Ferrony Bressan|first=Giuliano|date=September 2023|trans-title=Bodies and their worlds: from poetics to teaching|language=pt-BR|publisher=[[Federal University of Rio Grande do Sul]]}}</ref> They used their art to challenge gender and racial norms, making racial activism their primary cause.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Souza |first1=Victor Pereira de |last2=Bleicher |first2=Taís |first3=Breno de Castro |last3=Diniz |date=August 12, 2024 |title=Saúde mental e vivências fora dos binarismos de gênero entre jovens estudantes de graduação |url=https://seer.furg.br/divedu/article/view/17390 |journal=Diversidade e Educação |volume=12 |language=pt-BR |issue=1 |pages=296–321 |doi=10.14295/de.v12i1.17390 |issn=2358-8853 |archive-date=December 13, 2024 |access-date=June 7, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241213060105/https://seer.furg.br/divedu/article/view/17390 |url-status=live |trans-title=Mental health and experiences outside gender binaries among young undergraduate students}}</ref><ref>{{Cite thesis |last=Cavalcante |first=André |date=2021 |title=O corpo que habito: resistências e produção de sentidos dos/sobre os corpos trans |url=https://app.uff.br/riuff/bitstream/handle/1/22319/Tese%20Andr%E9%20Cavalcante.pdf?sequence=1 |institution= |language=pt-BR |archive-date=August 24, 2025 |access-date=June 7, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250824033140/https://app.uff.br/riuff/bitstream/handle/1/22319/Tese%20Andr%E9%20Cavalcante.pdf?sequence=1 |url-status= |publisher=[[Fluminense Federal University]]: Instituto De Letras|url-access=|trans-title=The body I inhabit: resistances and production of meanings of/about trans bodies}}</ref>

== Death and investigations ==
On April 29, 2018, Matheusa disappeared after leaving a party in the Encantado neighborhood,<ref name="revolução e amor" /> in the northern part of Rio de Janeiro. They were murdered by drug dealers in Morro do 18, in [[Quintino Bocaiuva, Rio de Janeiro|Quintino]].<ref name="G1"/> In July 2024, the principal defendant for the murder, Manuel Avelino de Sousa Junior, was sentenced to 18 years and four months of prison for the crimes of murder with a base motive and concealment of a corpse.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 25, 2024 |title=Caso Matheusa: traficante que matou estudante da Uerj é condenado a 18 anos de prisão |trans-title=Matheusa case: Drug trafficker who killed UERJ student sentenced to 18 years in prison |url=https://oglobo.globo.com/rio/noticia/2024/07/25/caso-matheusa-traficante-que-matou-estudante-da-uerj-e-condenado-a-18-anos-de-prisao.ghtml |access-date=September 2, 2026 |website=[[O Globo]] |language=pt-BR}}</ref>

== Legacy and tributes ==
Matheusa was portrayed in the documentary "{{Lang|pt|Sempre Verei Cores no seu Cinza}}", directed by filmmaker [[Anabela Roque]]. The film addresses the crisis at UERJ and shows the performance of students against the abandonment of the university.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Santos |first=Matheus Santa Rita dos |date=December 5, 2018 |title=Abraço |url=http://pantheon.ufrj.br/handle/11422/16678 |archive-date=June 8, 2026 |access-date=June 8, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260608054839/https://pantheon.ufrj.br/handle/11422/16678 |journal=Pantheon |url-status=live |trans-title=Hug|language=pt-BR}}</ref>

'''Matthew Greenfield''' (born 22nd January, 1995) is an American professional ice hockey goaltender for the [[Sheffield Steelers]], who play in the [[Elite Ice Hockey League|Elite Ice Hockey League (EIHL)]].<ref name="auto">{{Cite web |title=Matthew Greenfield – Sheffield Steelers |url=https://www.sheffieldsteelers.co.uk/player/matthew-greenfield/ |access-date=2026-06-11 |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Sheffield Steelers |url=https://www.eliteleague.co.uk/team/13-sheffield-steelers |access-date=2026-06-11 |website=EIHL |language=en}}</ref> He is currently signed until the end of the 2027-28 season after signing a three-year contract extension prior to the 2025-26 season.<ref name="auto"/> Greenfield started his junior career in the [[Ice hockey in the United States|United States]] and [[Ice hockey in Canada|Canada]], including playing for the [[University of Calgary]].<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web |title=Matthew Greenfield - Stats, Contract, Salary & More |url=https://www.eliteprospects.com/player/212972/matthew-greenfield |access-date=2026-06-11 |website=www.eliteprospects.com}}</ref> Greenfield reached the [[American Hockey League|American Hockey League (AHL)]], signing with the [[Springfield Thunderbirds]] in the 2018-19 season and the [[Stockton Heat]] in the 2021-22 season, both of which he never played a game; instead, playing with their [[ECHL]] counter-parts.<ref name="auto1"/>

After signing with the Sheffield Steelers in the 2022-23 season, Greenfield has become the most decorated goaltender in Steelers history after recording his 25th shutout in the 2025-26 season, beating Jody Lehman's previous record of 24.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Greenfield sets Steelers Shut Out Record – Sheffield Steelers |url=https://www.sheffieldsteelers.co.uk/greenfield-sets-steelers-shut-out-record/ |access-date=2026-06-11 |language=en-GB}}</ref> Greenfield won the Grand Slam with the Steelers in the 2023-24 season, winning the League, the Challenge Cup, and the Playoffs. He has also won EIHL Netminder of the Year three straight seasons in a row, being the 2022-23 season, the 2023-24 season, and the 2024-25 season, and has made the EIHL All-Star First Team twice, in the 2022-23 season and the 2023-24 season.<ref name="auto1"/>

== Playing career ==
Greenfield started his junior career in the US and Canada, playing in [[Florida]], [[Illinois]], [[Kitchener, Ontario|Kitchener]] and [[West Kelowna]]. He signed with the ECHL side [[Kansas City Mavericks]] for the 2020-21 season and again on a two-way deal with their [[American Hockey League|AHL]] team [[Stockton Heat]] for the 2021-22 season. 

=== Sheffield Steelers (2022 - present) ===
Greenfield joined the Steelers ahead of the [[2022–23 EIHL season|2022-23 EIHL Season]].<ref name="auto1"/> Since then, he has played in 229 games, winning 163 of them. He has recorded 25 shutouts, a 2.19 Goals Against Average (GAA), and an average save percentage of 92.28%.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Matthew Greenfield |url=https://www.eliteleague.co.uk/player/1714-matthew-greenfield |access-date=2026-06-11 |website=EIHL |language=en}}</ref>

'''Cortney Herron''' is a contemporary figurative painter and illustrator based in [[Los Angeles, California]].

== Early life and education ==
Herron was born and raised in Los Angeles, California.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Meet Cortney Herron |url=https://canvasrebel.com/meet-cortney-herron/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250311231258/https://canvasrebel.com/meet-cortney-herron/ |archive-date=2025-03-11 |access-date=2026-07-16 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Lee |first=Nathan |date=2026-02-18 |title=Cortney Herron to Exhibit at BUTTER Fine Art Fair in Los Angeles |url=https://lasentinel.net/cortney-herron-to-exhibit-at-butter-fine-art-fair-in-los-angeles.html |access-date=2026-07-22 |website=Los Angeles Sentinel |language=en-US}}</ref> She began painting at the age of three and continued to make art throughout high school. Herron attended the [[University of California, Davis]] where she obtained a degree in [[Communication design|Visual Communication Design]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2018-08-27 |title=Meet Cortney Herron - Voyage LA Magazine {{!}} LA City Guide |url=https://voyagela.com/interview/meet-cortney-herron/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260113032713/https://voyagela.com/interview/meet-cortney-herron/ |archive-date=2026-01-13 |access-date=2026-07-16 |website=voyagela.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Career ==
Herron's first full-time job after graduating from college was as a content manager for the online art marketplace Fine Art America. After working in this position for four years, Herron began to create art again while maintaining her day job.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Davidson |first=Sarah |date=2018-08-29 |title=A Room of Her Own |url=https://www.argonautnews.com/arts-events/a-room-of-her-own/article_a699b457-1fd7-5aa0-9b14-177c38628628.html |access-date=2026-07-16 |website=Argonaut News |language=en}}</ref> Herron left her position at Fine Art America after nearly seven years of employment and moved into the personal development industry.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-05-14 |title=Cortney Herron {{!}} Artist & Style Enthusiast – SHOUTOUT LA |url=https://shoutoutla.com/cortney-herron-artist-style-enthusiast/ |access-date=2026-07-16 |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2022, Herron's work was featured in [[Deep Space Gallery]] (77 Cornelison Ave.) as a part of “Mothership Connection,” an all-female art show.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McCall |first=Tris |date=2022-03-25 |title=“Mothership Connection” at Deep Space Gallery |url=https://jcitytimes.com/mothership-connection-at-deep-space-gallery/ |access-date=2026-07-16 |website=Jersey City Times |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2023, the Deep Space Gallery celebrated its seventh year of business by holding the show "777". Nearly every artist who had work featured in the gallery in previous years contributed to “777" culminating into a show of eighty-plus pieces. In accordance with the casino theme of the show, Herron contributed a painting of a ruminative gambler.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McCall |first=Tris |date=2023-08-04 |title=With “777,” Deep Space Gallery Deals Another Winning Hand |url=https://jcitytimes.com/with-777-deep-space-gallery-deals-another-winning-hand/ |access-date=2026-07-16 |website=Jersey City Times |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2023, Herron also shifted into being a full-time artist.<ref name=":1" />

From April 4 to 7 2024, Herron participated in [[Saatchi Art]]’s The Other Art Fair in Los Angeles, California.<ref>{{Cite news |last=The Other Art Fair |date=2024-03-11 |title=5 Artists To See at The Other Art Fair's Los Angeles Edition This April |url=https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2024/03/the-other-art-fair-los-angeles/ |access-date=2026-07-22 |work=Colossal |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2025, Cortney Herron, [[Julian Jamaal Jones]], and Sydneé Bethe collaborated with [[Pressed Juicery]]. The three artists were commissioned by Pressed Juicery to create artwork for their bottles in order to celebrate [[Black History Month]]. The special edition bottles were only sold in the month of February in 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-02-05 |title=8 Black History Month Food Collaborations To Get Excited About |url=https://www.delish.com/food-news/a63653556/black-history-month-food-collaborations-2025/ |access-date=2026-07-22 |website=Delish |language=en-US}}</ref> Herron provided the image of her painting titled "Bloom" for the special edition Citrus 2 bottle.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hall |first=Rashaun |date=2025-02-21 |title=Pressed Juicery Honors Black History Month With Limited Edition Artist Series |url=https://www.foodbeast.com/news/pressed-juicery-honors-black-history-month-with-limited-edition-artist-series/ |access-date=2026-07-22 |website=Foodbeast |language=en-US}}</ref>

Herron participated in the 2026 [[Ganggang|BUTTER Fine Art Fair]] in Los Angeles. The fair took place at [[Hollywood Park, Inglewood|Hollywood Park in Inglewood]] from February 28 to March 1, 2026.<ref name=":1" />

'''Milan Robin''' (born 24 November 1999) is a French footballer who plays as a central midfielder for [[Primeira Liga|Liga Portugal]] club [[G.D. Estoril Praia|Estoril Praia]].

== Club career ==
Robin is a product of the youth academies of the French clubs FC Eloyes, [[SAS Épinal|Épinal]] and [[FC Metz|Metz]]. He was first promoted to Metz's reserves in 2016, and on 15 July 2020 signed his first professional contract with the club.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.republicain-lorrain.fr/sport/2020/07/16/le-fc-metz-rattrape-milan-robin|title=Football | Formation. Le FC Metz rattrape Milan Robin|date=15 July 2020|website=www.republicain-lorrain.fr}}</ref> On 30 May 2021, he transferred to [[SO Cholet|Cholet]] in the [[Championnat National]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.vosgesmatin.fr/sport/2021/05/30/vosges-le-loya-milan-robin-quitte-metz-et-s-engage-a-cholet|title=Football/National. Vosges : le Loya Milan Robin quitte Metz et s’engage à Cholet|date=30 May 2021|website=www.vosgesmatin.fr}}</ref> Originally a [[winger (association football)|winger]], Robin suffered an injury in his first season at Cholet and was repositioned to midfielder.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.latribunemancelle.fr/article/milan-robin-la-perseverance-a-toute-epreuve|title=Milan Robin, la persévérance à toute épreuve|date=25 June 2025|website=La Tribune Mancelle}}</ref> On 31 July 2023, he moved to [[FC Martigues|Martigues]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.laprovence.com/article/sports/96933552805398/football-national-milan-robin-sengage-avec-le-fc-martigues?id=96933552805398|title=Football - National : Milan Robin s'engage avec le FC Martigues|date=31 July 2023|website=www.laprovence.com}}</ref> In his second season, he played a crucial role including the game-winning goal that promoted Martigues to [[Ligue 2]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://remiremontvallees.com/2024/05/19/football-ligue-2-enfant-du-fc-eloyes-milan-robin-et-le-fc-martigues-montent-en-ligue-2/|title=Football – Ligue 2 : enfant du FC Eloyes, Milan Robin et le FC Martigues montent en Ligue 2|first=La|last=rédaction|date=19 May 2024}}</ref> On 23 June 2025, he transferred to newly promoted [[Ligue 2]] side [[Le Mans FC]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.laprovence.com/article/sports/6361816171604214/football-national-apres-deux-saisons-a-martigues-milan-robin-signe-au-mans?id=6361816171604214|title=Football - National : après deux saisons à Martigues, Milan Robin signe au Mans|date=24 June 2025|website=www.laprovence.com}}</ref> He helped Le Mans earn promotion to [[Ligue 1]] for the 2026–27 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rfi.fr/en/sports/20260509-bastia-crowd-trouble-delays-le-mans-ligue-1-promotion-party|title=Bastia crowd trouble delays Le Mans Ligue 1 promotion party|date=9 May 2026|website=RFI}}</ref>

Robin announce official left for the Le Mans after one year.

On 4 September 2026, Robin abroad to Portugal for the first time and announce official transfer to [[Primeira Liga|Liga Portugal]] club, [[G.D. Estoril Praia|Estoril Praia]] for during 2026–27 season.

==International career==
Robin played for the [[France national under-16 football team|France U16]]s for a set of friendlies in 2014 and 2015.<ref name="auto"/>

He is currently playing for [[HC Spartak Moscow]] of the [[Kontinental Hockey League]] (KHL). He was previously selected by the [[Pittsburgh Penguins]] in the 7th round of the [[2017 NHL entry draft]] with the 217th overall pick, the last in the draft.{{Cite news | title=Penguins A to Z: Will Reilly’s progression has been limited |url=https://archive.triblive.com/sports/penguins-a-to-z-will-reillys-progression-has-been-limited/ |date = July 7, 2022 | website=[[TribLive]] }} ==Playing career== ===Junior=== Reilly was born in [[Toronto]] and played high school hockey at the [[Upper Canada College]], then played one game for the [[Oakville Blades]] and a full season for the [[North York Rangers]] in the [[Ontario Junior Hockey League]] and was named to the 2015 First All-Prospect Team.{{Cite news | title=Rangers’ Reilly named 1st Team All-Prospect|url=https://www.northyorkrangersjra.com/rangers-reilly-named-1st-team-all-prospect |date = February 24, 2015 | website=[[North York Rangers]] }} He then played one season for the [[Nanaimo Clippers]] in the [[British Columbia Hockey League]] before committing to play for the [[RPI Engineers men's ice hockey|Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute Engineers]] in 2016.{{Cite news | title=Reilly headed to RPI |url=https://bchl.ca/reilly-headed-to-rpi |date = April 18, 2016 | website=[[British Columbia Hockey League]] }} He played four seasons for RPI, scoring 75 (21+54) points in 105 games. He was the team's [[alternate captain]] in his junior season and the [[captain (ice hockey)|captain]] in his senior.{{Cite news | title=Former RPI Captain Will Reilly '20 Helps Florida Everblades Win ECHL Kelly Cup |url=https://rpiathletics.com/news/2024/6/10/former-rpi-captain-will-reilly-helps-florida-everblades-win-echl-kelly-cup.aspx |date = June 10, 2024 | website=[[Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute Engineers]] }} He was also named to [[ECAC Hockey]]'s second all-star team and nominated for the [[ECAC Hockey Best Defensive Defenseman]] award.{{Cite news | title=Pittsburgh Penguins Sign Defenseman William Reilly To 2-Year Entry-Level Contract |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/pittsburgh/news/pittsburgh-penguins-sign-defenseman-william-reilly/|date = April 15, 2020 | website=[[CBS News]] }} ===Professional === After going undrafted his first two years of eligibility, Reilly was selected by the [[Pittsburgh Penguins]] in the 7th round of the [[2017 NHL entry draft]] with the 217th overall pick, the last in the draft, after his first NCAA season.{{Cite news | title=Penguins take defenceman Will Reilly with last pick in 2017 NHL Draft |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/hockey/nhl/penguins-take-defenceman-will-reilly-last-pick-2017-nhl-draft/ |date = June 24, 2017 | website=[[Sportsnet]] }} The Penguins signed him for a two-year, entry-level contract on April 15, 2020. He did not play in the NHL, and recorded 13 (6+7) points in 72 games with the [[Wilkes-Barre/Scranton Penguins]], Pittsburgh's [[American Hockey League]] farm club and 6 (2+4) points in 3 games with their [[ECHL]] affiliate [[Wheeling Nailers]]. At the end of the contract, he did not receive a qualifying offer from the Penguins. In the 2022-23 season, he played for the [[Tucson Roadrunners]] in the [[American Hockey League]] (AHL) and scored 5 (1+4) points in 30 games. For the 2023-24 season, he signed a contract with the [[Charlotte Checkers]] in the AHL.{{Cite news | title=Checkers sign Reilly, Khodorenko |url=https://theahl.com/news/checkers-sign-reilly-khodorenko |date = August 7, 2023 | website=[[American Hockey League]] }} He scored no points one game for Charlotte and primarily played with the [[Florida Everblades]] in the ECHL, recording 38 (10+28) points in 55 regular season games and 11 (3+8) in 22 playoff games on the team's run to their third consecutive [[Kelly Cup]] championship. For the 2024-25 season, Reilly went overseas for the first time and joined [[HC Motor České Budějovice]] in the [[Czech Extraliga]].{{Cite news | title=Kanadský obránce Reilly novou posilou Motoru! |url=https://hcmotor.cz/clanek.asp?id=Kanadsky-obrance-Reilly-novou-posilou-Motoru-12489 |date = June 10, 2024 | website=[[HC Motor České Budějovice]] |language=Czech}} He recorded 12 (5+7) points in 55 games with the team. For the 2025-26 season, he joined the [[Shanghai Dragons]] in the [[Kontinental Hockey League]] on a one-year contract.{{Cite news | title=More Dragons on the Ice! Groleau, Valentsov, Reilly, Parker and Spencer Foo Sign with Shanghai Dragons |url=https://hc-dragons.com/en/news/more-dragons-on-the-ice-groleau-valentsov-reilly-parker-and-spencer-foo-sign-with-shanghai-dragons/ |date = August 18, 2025 | website=[[Shanghai Dragons]] }} In his first KHL season, he scored 18 (4+14) games in 64 games. On July 21, 2026 he signed a two-year contract with [[HC Spartak Moscow]].{{Cite news | title=Новичком «Спартака» стал защитник Уилл Райлли, подписан контракт на два года |url=https://spartak.ru/news/novichkom-spartaka-stal-zashhitnik-uill-rajlli-podpisan-kontrakt-na-dva-goda/ |date = July 21, 2026 | website=[[HC Spartak Moscow]] |language=Russian}} == Career statistics == {| border="0" cellpadding="1" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:center; width:60em;" |- bgcolor="#e0e0e0" ! colspan="3" bgcolor="#ffffff"| ! rowspan="99" bgcolor="#ffffff"| ! colspan="5"|[[Regular season]] ! rowspan="99" bgcolor="#ffffff"| ! colspan="5"|[[Playoffs]] |- bgcolor="#e0e0e0" ! '''Ikkei Nitta''' ({{langx|ja|新田一景}}; born 23 April 1998) is a Japanese water polo player who plays as a centre back. He represents Japan internationally and competed at the [[2024 Summer Olympics]]. He won gold medals with Japan at the [[2022 Asian Games]] and [[2026 Asian Games]].<ref name="JOC">{{cite web |title=新田 一景 |trans-title=Ikkei Nitta |url=https://www.joc.or.jp/athletes/nittaikkei/index.html |website=[[Japanese Olympic Committee]] |language=ja |access-date=7 October 2026}}</ref><ref name="TBS">{{cite web |title=〖選手一覧〗水球 足立聖弥・有馬優美・稲場晴香など 日本代表選手 〖アジア大会2026〗 |trans-title=Water polo national team players at the 2026 Asian Games |url=https://newsdig.tbs.co.jp/articles/-/2828144 |publisher=TBS NEWS DIG |language=ja |access-date=7 October 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-10-03 |title=【愛知・名古屋アジア大会】水球男子、日本が「金」 {{!}} 岐阜新聞デジタル |url=https://www.gifu-np.co.jp/articles/-/778931 |access-date=2026-10-07 |website=【愛知・名古屋アジア大会】水球男子、日本が「金」 {{!}} 岐阜新聞デジタル |language=ja}}</ref>

== Career ==

Nitta was born in [[Ishikawa Prefecture]] and attended Kanazawa Municipal Technical High School, where he served as captain of the men's water polo team. He led the school to victory at the national high school championships and subsequently attended Niigata Sangyo University.<ref name="Ishikawa">{{cite web |title=石川県出身として初めての水球男子五輪代表！新田一景選手がパリ内定を決める |trans-title=Ikkei Nitta becomes the first men's water polo Olympian from Ishikawa Prefecture |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Eh9MB6GDM2M |date=22 April 2024 |publisher=Ishikawa TV |language=ja |access-date=7 October 2026}}</ref><ref name="JOC"/>

After graduating from university, Nitta joined Bourbon Water Polo Club Kashiwazaki and became a member of the Japanese national team. He developed into a regular centre-back for Japan and competed in major international tournaments.<ref name="TVAsahi">{{cite web |title=新田 一景｜日本代表選手｜世界水泳シンガポール2025 |trans-title=Ikkei Nitta – Japan national team player |url=https://www.tv-asahi.co.jp/swimming/sekaisuiei2025/player/wp/m_nitta_ikkei.html |publisher=TV Asahi |language=ja |access-date=7 October 2026}}</ref>

Nitta represented Japan at the [[2022 Asian Games]], which were held in Hangzhou in 2023 after being postponed. Japan won the men's water polo tournament, defeating China in the final to claim the gold medal. Nitta was part of the Japanese squad that won the country's first Asian Games men's water polo title in 53 years.<ref name="JOCHangzhou">{{cite web |title=新田 一景 |trans-title=Ikkei Nitta |url=https://www.joc.or.jp/games/asia/2022/japan/waterpolo/team/nittaikkei.html |website=[[Japanese Olympic Committee]] |language=ja |access-date=7 October 2026}}</ref><ref name="Ishikawa"/>

In 2024, Nitta was selected for Japan's men's water polo team at the [[2024 Summer Olympics]] in [[Paris]]. Japan finished 11th in the men's tournament after being eliminated in the preliminary round.<ref name="JOCParis">{{cite web |title=新田 一景｜水泳／水球｜パリ2024 |trans-title=Ikkei Nitta – Swimming/Water Polo – Paris 2024 |url=https://www.joc.or.jp/games/olympic/paris/sports/waterpolo/team/nittaikkei.html |website=[[Japanese Olympic Committee]] |language=ja |access-date=7 October 2026}}</ref><ref name="Niigata">{{cite web |title=パリ2024オリンピック夏季競技大会に出場した新潟県関係選手の大会結果を紹介します |trans-title=Results of Niigata-related athletes at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games |url=https://www.pref.niigata.lg.jp/sec/kenminsports/paris2024olympic.html |publisher=Niigata Prefecture |language=ja |access-date=7 October 2026}}</ref>

In January 2025, Nitta represented Japan at the [[2025 World Aquatics Men's Water Polo World Cup|World Aquatics Men's Water Polo World Cup Division 1]] in Romania. Japan finished sixth in the tournament and qualified for the World Cup final tournament. Nitta competed as a member of Bourbon Water Polo Club Kashiwazaki.<ref name="KashiwazakiWC">{{cite web |title=水球ワールドカップで日本男子が6位！世界一決定戦への出場権獲得！―ブルボンKZ新田選手・稲場選手が出場 |trans-title=Japan's men's water polo team finishes sixth at World Cup and qualifies for the final tournament |url=https://www.city.kashiwazaki.lg.jp/suikyunomachi_kz/bourbonwaterpoloclub/44321.html |date=17 January 2025 |publisher=Kashiwazaki City |language=ja |access-date=7 October 2026}}</ref>

Later in 2025, Nitta was selected for Japan's squad at the [[2025 World Aquatics Championships]] in Singapore. He was listed as a field player and represented Bourbon Water Polo Club Kashiwazaki.<ref name="Worlds2025">{{cite web |title=世界選手権［水球］（2025/シンガポール）メンバー |trans-title=2025 World Championships water polo team members |url=https://aquatics.or.jp/tournament/member/52484/ |publisher=Japan Aquatics |language=ja |access-date=7 October 2026}}</ref><ref name="KashiwazakiWorlds">{{cite web |title=水球のまち柏崎から3選手と監督が水球日本代表に選出！―第22回世界水泳選手権 |trans-title=Three players from Kashiwazaki's water polo club selected for Japan's national team at the 22nd World Aquatics Championships |url=https://www.city.kashiwazaki.lg.jp/suikyunomachi_kz/bourbonwaterpoloclub/46155.html |date=7 July 2025 |publisher=Kashiwazaki City |language=ja |access-date=7 October 2026}}</ref>

In 2026, Nitta was selected for Japan's men's water polo team at the [[2026 Asian Games]] in Aichi-Nagoya. He was listed as a centre-back and represented Bourbon Water Polo Club Kashiwazaki.<ref name="AsianGames2026">{{cite web |title=第20回アジア競技大会（2026/愛知・名古屋）[水球]メンバー |trans-title=20th Asian Games 2026 Aichi-Nagoya water polo team members |url=https://aquatics.or.jp/tournament/member/60829/ |publisher=Japan Aquatics |language=ja |access-date=7 October 2026}}</ref>

Nitta scored twice in Japan's opening match of the Asian Games, a 19–11 victory over Kazakhstan on 26 September. He also scored in Japan's 30–6 win over Hong Kong in the group stage and contributed to the team's progression to the knockout rounds.<ref name="AsianResults">{{cite web |title=第20回アジア競技大会（2026/愛知・名古屋）[水球] |trans-title=20th Asian Games 2026 Aichi-Nagoya water polo results |url=https://aquatics.or.jp/tournament/58380/ |publisher=Japan Aquatics |language=ja |access-date=7 October 2026}}</ref>

Japan defeated Singapore 32–8 in the quarter-final and Iran 26–12 in the semi-final before facing Kazakhstan in the final. On 3 October 2026, Japan defeated Kazakhstan 24–7 to win the gold medal and successfully defend its Asian Games title.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Казахстан завоевал серебро в водном поло на Азиаде-2026 {{!}} Спортивный портал Vesti.kz |url=https://vesti.kz/asiada/matche-kazahstan-yaponiya-reshilas-sudba-zolota-aziadyi-2026-388935 |access-date=2026-10-07 |website=vesti.kz}}</ref> Nitta scored twice in the final and finished the tournament as one of Japan's contributors in attack.<ref name="AsianFinal">{{cite web |title=〖男子水球〗カザフスタンに勝利した日本が2大会連続5回目の優勝を果たす（第20回アジア競技大会） |trans-title=Men's water polo: Japan defeats Kazakhstan to win its second consecutive and fifth overall Asian Games title |url=https://aquatics.or.jp/topics/65004/ |date=3 October 2026 |publisher=Japan Aquatics |language=ja |access-date=7 October 2026}}</ref> The victory gave Nitta his second Asian Games gold medal and helped Japan win its fifth men's water polo title at the Asian Games.<ref name="JOC"/><ref>{{Cite web |title=【男子水球】カザフスタンに勝利した日本が2大会連続5回目の優勝を果たす（第20回アジア競技大会） ｜ Japan Aquatics MAG |url=https://aquatics.or.jp/topics/65004/ |access-date=2026-10-07 |language=ja}}</ref>

'''Giovana Vito Mondardo''' (born 1 February 1993) is a Brazilian politician who was elected member of the [[Chamber of Deputies (Brazil)|Chamber of Deputies]] in 2026.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://g1.globo.com/sc/santa-catarina/eleicoes/2026/noticia/2026/10/04/eleicoes-2026-giovana-mondardo-pcdob-e-eleita-deputada-federal-por-santa-catarina.ghtml|title=Eleições 2026: Giovana Mondardo (PCdoB) é eleita deputada federal por Santa Catarina|work=[[g1 (website)|g1]]|date=4 October 2026|language=pt}}</ref> She has been a municipal councillor of [[Criciúma]] since 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://horadopovo.com.br/giovana-se-elege-em-sc-e-quer-um-projeto-nacional-de-desenvolvimento-e-lula-na-cabeca/|title=Giovana se elege em SC e quer "um projeto nacional de desenvolvimento". "É Lula na cabeça!"|work=[[:pt:Hora do Povo|Hora do Povo]]|date=6 October 2026|language=pt}}</ref>
